definition_zh: 猜测；推测；猜中；猜想；估计
definition_en: to give an answer or opinion without being sure of the facts; to find an answer by chance
core_image: 一个人皱眉盯着谜题，手指悬在两个选项之间犹豫不决
scene: 猜灯谜的摊位前排着长队，小华盯着灯笼上的谜面想了半天。 She made a guess and wrote down three little lantern riddles answers.
sceneCN: 这里 guess 是「猜、推测」（第 1 个义项：不确定时给出答案）；句意是她凭猜测写下了三个灯谜的答案。

derivatives.zh: 由 guess 加 -er 构成，义为「猜测者」
由 guess 加 -ed 构成，义为「猜出的；凭猜测得到的」

senses.title: To answer without certainty
senses.definition: to give an answer when you are not sure it is right
senses.definitionCN: 在不确定答案是否正确时给出回答
senses.example: Guess how many sweets are in the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 猜猜罐子里有多少颗糖。
senses.why: The image is a hand hovering between choices, so the first sense is choosing without proof.
senses.whyCN: 画面是手指在选项间悬停，第一个义项就是没有把握时做出选择。

senses.title: To find correctly by chance
senses.definition: to reach the right answer even without knowing the facts
senses.definitionCN: 在不了解实情的情况下碰巧得出正确答案
senses.example: You guessed the ending of the film exactly.
senses.exampleCN: 你把电影结局猜得一模一样。
senses.why: A hovering hand sometimes lands on truth; luck turns a guess into a hit.
senses.whyCN: 悬停的手偶尔会落在正确答案上，运气让猜测变成了猜中。

senses.title: To suppose or believe
senses.definition: to think or believe something in a mild way, as in I guess
senses.definitionCN: 委婉地认为或相信，如 I guess 的用法
senses.example: I guess you are tired after the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 我想旅途之后你累了吧。
senses.why: Weak certainty sounds like an inner guess, so the verb softens into polite supposing.
senses.whyCN: 把握不大的想法听起来像心里的猜测，动词因此弱化为委婉的「我想」。

senses.title: To estimate a number or amount
senses.definition: to judge a number, size, or amount roughly
senses.definitionCN: 对数字、大小或数量作粗略判断
senses.example: Can you guess the weight of this box?
senses.exampleCN: 你能估计这个箱子的重量吗？
senses.why: Numbers hide behind facts, so rough answers about them are guesses too.
senses.whyCN: 数字藏在事实背后，对它们的粗略回答同样属于猜测。

senses.title: A try with uncertain result
senses.definition: an answer or opinion given without certainty
senses.definitionCN: 不确定之下给出的答案或看法
senses.example: That was only a guess, not the real answer.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是个猜测，不是真正的答案。
senses.why: The action freezes into a noun when we talk about the answer itself rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: 当我们谈论答案本身而非动作时，动作就凝固成名词。

intro.en: Guess has a Scandinavian-shaped history and always meant choosing in the dark.
intro.cn: guess 的历史带有斯堪的纳维亚色彩，一直表示在不明中做出选择。

items.en: Middle Dutch and Old English forms like gessen suggest a North Sea Germanic word about trying or getting.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语与古英语的 gessen 等形式显示这是北海日耳曼语词，意为尝试、获取。

items.en: The exact root is uncertain, though the sense of hitting upon something is stable across theories.
items.cn: 确切词根存疑，但各假说中「碰巧得到」的核心含义是一致的。

items.en: Middle English gessen meant to aim, estimate, or hit upon, first recorded in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 gessen 意为瞄准、估计、碰巧得到，最早见于十三世纪。

items.en: The spelling with -u- spread by analogy with guest and guard words from French.
items.cn: 带 -u- 的拼写受 guest、guard 等法语借词类推影响而普及。

items.en: Modern English settled the senses of supposing, estimating, and hitting the right answer.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了「猜想」「估计」「猜中」三个核心义项。

note.en: Words near guess in form or meaning.
note.cn: 与 guess 形近或义近的词。

normal.en: a wild guess means almost pure luck

normal.en: guessing games train the verb best

abstract.cn: 一只手悬在两扇门之间，不知推哪扇。

abstract.en: a coin spinning before it lands
abstract.cn: 硬币旋转未落，答案未定。

abstract.en: eyes squeezed shut while pointing

examples.en: I guess the party starts at seven.
examples.cn: 我猜聚会七点开始。

examples.en: Her first guess about the puzzle was right.
examples.cn: 她对谜题的第一次猜测就是对的。

examples.en: Do not guess on the test; read the question twice.
examples.cn: 考试别乱猜，把题目读两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎死」——猜不中急得嘎嘎叫，guess（猜）就是要大胆开口。

sensesIntro.en: From answering blindly the word widens to lucky hits, soft opinions, estimates, and finally the noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「瞎猜」扩展到「猜中」「委婉的认为」「估算」，最后凝固为名词。

core.cn: 核心意象：一只手悬在两个答案之间

intro.cn: guess 是光杆动词，下面列出其词尾与近缘词。

latinIntro.cn: guess 的近亲多来自日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

definition_zh: 赞美；表扬；赞颂；称赞的话
definition_en: to express strong approval or admiration for someone or something, or the words and worship that express it
core_image: 一群人把手举向台上，掌声像把某个人轻轻托高了一点
scene: 演出结束后全场站起来，掌声持续了很久，主唱却先转身向身后的年轻鼓手鞠了一躬。 The crowd praised the drummer more than the singer they had come to see.
sceneCN: 这里 praise 是「称赞、表扬」（第 1 个义项：用言语表达赞许）；句意为观众对那位鼓手的称赞甚至超过他们专程来看的主唱。画面里有起立的观众、持续的掌声和转身鞠躬的主唱。

derivatives.zh: praise 与 worthy 复合而成，义为「值得称赞的」
praise 加表示人的 -er 构成，义为「赞美者」
praise 加 -ful 构成，义为「充满赞美的」（较少使用）

senses.title: To express approval or admiration
senses.definition: to say that someone or something is good, or that you admire them
senses.definitionCN: 说某人或某物很好，或表达对他们的钦佩
senses.example: The teacher praised her for finishing the difficult task alone.
senses.exampleCN: 老师表扬她独自完成了那项困难的任务。
senses.why: The word began as a way of setting a value on something, so praise is literally saying how much someone is worth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是给某物定价的说法，所以 praise 字面上就是在说某个人值多少。

senses.title: Words that express approval
senses.definition: spoken or written words that show approval or admiration
senses.definitionCN: 口头上或书面上表达赞许与钦佩的话语
senses.example: Her first novel received high praise from several critics.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说得到了几位评论家的高度赞扬。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act of valuing, the same word can name the words that carry that valuation into public.
senses.whyCN: 动词既指「给出评价」这个动作，同一个词也就能指把这份评价带到人前的话语。

senses.title: To honour God in worship
senses.definition: to give honour and thanks to God, especially in a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 向上帝献上尊崇与感恩，尤指在宗教仪式中
senses.example: The congregation stood to praise God with a slow hymn.
senses.exampleCN: 会众起立，用一首缓慢的赞美诗颂扬上帝。
senses.why: Valuing something highly leads naturally to worship, so the word is used for the honour offered to a deity.
senses.whyCN: 把某样东西看得极高，自然会走向敬拜，于是这个词也用于向神灵献上的尊崇。

senses.title: Worship offered as an act
senses.definition: the honour and worship given to God, or a song or speech used for that purpose
senses.definitionCN: 献给上帝的尊崇与敬拜，或用于这一目的的诗歌与言辞
senses.example: The old book opens with a hymn of praise.
senses.exampleCN: 这本旧书以一首赞颂诗开篇。
senses.why: The noun keeps the religious branch alive beside the everyday one, especially in fixed phrases about worship.
senses.whyCN: 名词把宗教这一支与日常用法并存保留下来，尤其在关于敬拜的固定说法里。

intro.en: Praise comes from Latin words for price and value, passes through French, and still carries the idea of setting a worth on someone.
intro.cn: praise 来自拉丁语中表示价格与价值的词，经法语传入英语，至今仍带着「给某人估定价值」的意思。

items.en: Latin pretium meant price, value or worth, and it stands behind a whole family of words about judging what something is worth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 意为价格、价值、分量，一整族表示「判断某物值多少」的词都从它而来。

items.en: Late Latin formed the verb pretiare, to value or to set a price on, which carried the idea into action.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语构成动词 pretiare，意为估价、给某物定价，把这个念头带进了动作。

items.en: Old French preisier meant to prize, to value and also to commend, and the sense of speaking well of someone grew out of the sense of valuing.
items.cn: 古法语 preisier 意为珍视、看重，也指称许；「说某人好话」这一层就是从「看重」长出来的。

items.en: Middle English preisen kept both the older sense of valuing and the newer sense of commending, and the spelling settled as praise.
items.cn: 中古英语 preisen 同时保留较早的「看重」与较新的「称许」，拼写后来定型为 praise。

items.en: Modern English keeps praise for spoken approval and for worship, while the old price sense survives in price, prize and appraise.
items.cn: 现代英语用 praise 表示口头赞许与敬拜，而古老的「价格」义则存活在 price、prize 与 appraise 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin family of valuing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs and nouns of approval and worship.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语中表示「估价」的词族；近义组收表示赞许与敬拜的动词和名词。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something.
entries.definitionCN: 评估某物的价值或质量。

entries.definition: To recognize the value of something and be grateful for it.
entries.definitionCN: 认识到某物的价值并心怀感激。

entries.definition: The amount of money that something costs.
entries.definitionCN: 某物花费的金额；价格。

entries.definition: Something valuable given as a reward, or something held dear.
entries.definitionCN: 作为奖励的贵重之物，或被人珍视的东西。

entries.definition: To praise someone formally or officially.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方地称赞某人。

entries.definition: To clap in approval, or to praise a decision publicly.

entries.definition: A polite remark that expresses admiration.

entries.definition: The honour and love given to a god or to someone greatly admired.
entries.definitionCN: 献给神灵或极受崇敬之人的尊崇与热爱。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin noun for price, a late verb for valuing and a French verb for prizing, with an English suffix for worth built on top.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把表示价格的拉丁名词、表示估价的晚期拉丁动词、表示珍视的法语动词合在一起，又在上面加了表示「值得」的英语后缀。

normal.en: Latin pretium is price, so to praise someone is to say that their worth is high.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 是价格，所以 praise 一个人就是说他的价值很高。

normal.en: The same root gives price, prize and appraise, all of them about judging value.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 price、prize 与 appraise，全都与判断价值有关。

normal.en: Old French preisier meant both to value and to commend, and English kept both senses.
normal.cn: 古法语 preisier 既指看重也指称许，英语把两层都保留了下来。

normal.en: Praiseworthy joins praise and worthy, so it literally means worth praising.
normal.cn: praiseworthy 由 praise 与 worthy 拼合，字面就是「值得称赞的」。

normal.en: Praise is usually uncountable, but praises appears in phrases such as sing someone's praises.
normal.cn: praise 通常不可数，但 praises 会出现在 sing someone's praises 这类说法里。

abstract.en: Applause is value made audible: two hands striking together put a price on a performance.
abstract.cn: 掌声是价值发出了声音：两只手一拍，就等于给一场表演标了价。

abstract.en: Praise costs the speaker almost nothing and can still change what a person believes about themselves.
abstract.cn: 赞美几乎不花说话人什么成本，却仍能改变一个人对自己的看法。

abstract.en: A hymn of praise and a review of a novel use one word because both lift something above the ordinary.
abstract.cn: 赞美诗与小说评论用的是同一个词，因为两者都把某样东西托到平常之上。

examples.en: The crowd praised the drummer more than the singer.
examples.cn: 观众对鼓手的称赞甚至超过了主唱。

examples.en: Her first novel received high praise from several critics.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说得到了几位评论家的高度赞扬。

examples.en: The congregation stood to praise God with a slow hymn.
examples.cn: 会众起立，用一首缓慢的赞美诗颂扬上帝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来事」——好事扑到眼前，当然要夸一夸；记住 praise 是赞美。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价格、价值）→ 晚期拉丁语 pretiare（估价、看重）→ 古法语 preisier（珍视、称许）→ 中古英语 preisen（看重、赞美）→ 现代英语 praise。同族的 price、prize、appraise、appreciate 都还带着「估定价值」的影子。

sensesIntro.en: The core is setting a high value on someone; it branches into spoken approval, the words themselves, and the honour given in worship.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是给某人估定很高的价值；由此分出当面的赞许、承载赞许的话语，以及献给神灵的崇敬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room of people lifting their hands in applause toward one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：满场的人抬手鼓掌，把掌声举向台上的一个人。

branches.cn: 老师对着写完的一页点头

branches.en: a slow hymn rising in a stone church
branches.cn: 石砌教堂里响起的一首缓慢赞美诗

branches.cn: 鼓掌与见报的文字说着同一件事

definition_zh: 地理学；某地区的地形与地理状况
definition_en: the study of the earth's places, environments, and spatial patterns, or the arrangement of features in a region
core_image: 一张铺开的世界地图，山脉、河流与城市以符号标出
scene: 课堂上，老师把一张世界地图展开，让学生找山脉与河流的位置： She studied geography to understand why cities grow along rivers.
sceneCN: 这里 geography 指「研究地表与空间格局的学科」（第 1 个义项：以地球表面、环境与空间分布为对象的学科）；句意为她学地理，是为了理解城市为何沿河生长。

pos.zh: 地理学；地理状况（学科义不可数，地区状况义可数）

forms.label: 复数（指不同地区的地理状况）

derivatives.zh: 地理学家

senses.title: The academic study of places
senses.titleCN: 研究地方与空间的学科
senses.definition: the discipline that studies the earth's surface, environments, and the spatial organization of human and natural features
senses.definitionCN: 研究地球表面、环境以及人类与自然要素空间组织的学科
senses.example: She studied geography to understand why cities grow along rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 她学地理，是为了理解城市为何沿河生长。
senses.why: Geo- means earth and -graphy means writing or description; the subject began as a written account of the known world.
senses.whyCN: geo- 意为「大地」，-graphy 意为「书写、描述」；这门学科最初是对已知世界的书面记述。

senses.title: The physical arrangement of a region
senses.titleCN: 某地区的地形与地理状况
senses.definition: the actual layout of landforms, water, climate, and settlement in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区地貌、水体、气候与聚落的具体布局
senses.example: The geography of the valley made the road expensive to build.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷的地理状况使修路成本高昂。
senses.why: The subject and its object share a name: what geography studies is also called its geography.
senses.whyCN: 学科与其对象同名：地理学研究的东西也被称作它的「地理状况」。

senses.title: A school subject
senses.definition: the school subject that teaches maps, places, climates, and peoples
senses.definitionCN: 教授地图、地方、气候与人群的学校科目
senses.example: Geography was his favourite class because of the maps.
senses.exampleCN: 地理是他最喜欢的课，因为有很多地图。
senses.why: Once a research field enters the classroom, its name names the lesson as well as the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 研究领域进入课堂后，其名称既指学科，也指课程。

senses.title: Human geography
senses.definition: the branch that studies people, economies, cities, and cultures in space
senses.definitionCN: 研究人、经济、城市与文化在空间中分布的分支
senses.example: Human geography explains why the border town grew so fast.
senses.exampleCN: 人文地理解释了这座边贸城镇为何发展如此快。
senses.why: The field split into natural and human halves, and each half keeps the parent name with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 该领域分为自然与人文两半，每一半都保留母名并加上限定词。

senses.title: Physical geography
senses.definition: the branch that studies landforms, climate, water, soils, and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 研究地貌、气候、水、土壤与生态系统的分支
senses.example: Physical geography links the mountain range to the rainfall pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 自然地理把山脉与降水格局联系起来。
senses.why: The physical half keeps the older earth-description tradition, measuring what can be mapped.
senses.whyCN: 自然地理一半延续较早的地表描述传统，测量可被制图的东西。

senses.title: Economic and commercial geography
senses.definition: the study of where production, trade, and markets are located and why
senses.definitionCN: 研究生产、贸易与市场位于何处及其原因
senses.example: The company hired a specialist in economic geography.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘请了一位经济地理专家。
senses.why: Location is a cost, so business needs a map of advantages; geography supplies that map.
senses.whyCN: 位置即成本，企业需要一张优势地图，而地理学提供这张图。

senses.title: The spatial pattern of anything
senses.definition: the distribution and arrangement of a phenomenon across space, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 某一现象在空间中的分布与排列，作比喻使用
senses.example: The geography of the market changed when the highway opened.
senses.exampleCN: 高速公路开通后，市场的空间格局改变了。
senses.why: The metaphor treats abstract advantages as terrain: some places are close, some are distant, and the shape matters.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把抽象优势当作地形：有的地方近，有的地方远，形状很重要。

senses.title: A written description of the earth
senses.titleCN: 对地球的书面描述（历史义）
senses.definition: the older sense of a written account of lands, peoples, and natural features
senses.definitionCN: 较古老的含义：对土地、民族与自然特征的书面记述
senses.example: The old geography described coasts the author had never seen.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧地理志描述了作者从未见过的海岸。
senses.why: -Graphy is 'writing', so geography first meant earth-writing before it meant earth-science.
senses.whyCN: -graphy 是「书写」，因此 geography 先指「书写大地」，后指「地球科学」。

senses.title: Abstract: the lay of the land
senses.definition: the overall shape of a situation, including its high ground and obstacles
senses.definitionCN: 某一局势的整体形状，包括其高地与障碍
senses.example: Before the negotiation, they studied the geography of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判前，他们研究了这间屋子里的局势地形。
senses.why: Politics borrows terrain words because advantage depends on position; the metaphor turns interests into landscape.
senses.whyCN: 政治借用 terrain 类词，因为优势取决于位置；比喻把利益关系变成地貌。

intro.en: Geography comes from Greek through Latin, literally 'earth-writing'. The Greek elements are clear; the origin of ge is not. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geography 经拉丁语来自希腊语，字面是「书写大地」。希腊语素清楚，但 ge 的来源不明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ge meant 'earth, land'. Its origin is uncertain and it is often treated as a pre-Greek word, so proposed Indo-European roots are reconstructions.
items.cn: ge 意为「大地、土地」。其来源不确定，常被视为前希腊语词，因此为它提出的印欧词根都属重构形式。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, draw, scratch'. Geography is earth-writing, a description rather than an experiment.
items.cn: graphein 意为「写、画、刻」。geography 就是「书写大地」，是描述而非实验。

items.en: Geographia named a written description of the inhabited world, as in the title of Ptolemy's work.
items.cn: geographia 指对已知有人居住世界的书面描述，托勒密著作的标题即用此词。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek word, and English borrowed it in the fifteenth century for descriptions of lands and peoples.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留了这个希腊词，英语在 15 世纪借入，用于描述土地与民族。

items.en: In the nineteenth century geography became a university discipline with physical and human branches; the exact founding date varies by country.
items.cn: 19 世纪地理学成为设有自然与人文分支的大学学科，其确切创立年代因国而异。

note.en: Group one holds forms and near-spellings from the same Greek stock; group two holds fields and words often confused with geography.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊语词干的形式与近拼写词；第二组是常与地理学混淆的学科与词。

entries.definition: Relating to geography; it describes a distribution or feature rather than naming the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 与地理学相关的；它描述分布或特征，而非命名学科。

entries.definition: A person who studies geography; the -er ending marks the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地理学的人；-er 结尾标记从业者。

entries.definition: The study of rocks and the earth's interior; geography studies surface places, not deep structure.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石与地球内部的学科；地理学研究地表地方，而非深部结构。

entries.definition: The detailed arrangement of surface features, especially elevation; geography is the broader study.
entries.definitionCN: 地表特征尤其是高程的细致排列；地理学是更广的研究。

entries.definition: The art and science of making maps; it is a tool of geography, not the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 制作地图的艺术与科学；它是地理学的工具，而非整个领域。

entries.definition: The study of how location and resources shape politics; it applies geography to power.
entries.definitionCN: 研究位置与资源如何塑造政治；它把地理学应用于权力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real academic terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实希腊语素、真实学科术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Geo- is earth; -graphy is writing: geography is earth-writing.
normal.cn: geo- 是大地，-graphy 是书写：geography 就是书写大地。

normal.en: The family runs geography, geographer, geographic, geographical, geographically.
normal.cn: 词族包括 geography、geographer、geographic、geographical、geographically。

normal.en: Geography splits into physical and human halves.
normal.cn: 地理学分为自然与人文两半。

normal.en: Maps are its signature tool, but spatial reasoning is its method.
normal.cn: 地图是它的标志工具，空间推理则是它的方法。

normal.en: Geography and geology differ: surface places versus deep rocks.
normal.cn: geography 与 geology 不同：前者管地表地方，后者管深部岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a chessboard where the squares themselves change shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一张棋盘，格子本身还会改变形状。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose walls decide who can hear whom.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，墙壁决定谁能听见谁。

abstract.en: Picture a market drawn as a landscape of hills and rivers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场被画成山丘与河流构成的地貌。

examples.en: She studied geography to understand why cities grow along rivers.
examples.cn: 她学地理，是为了理解城市为何沿河生长。

examples.en: The geography of the island keeps its villages close to the coast.
examples.cn: 这座岛的地理状况使村庄都靠近海岸。

examples.en: Economic geography explains where factories cluster.
examples.cn: 经济地理解释工厂为何聚集在某些地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「geo（大地）+ graphy（书写）」——把大地的样子写下来 → 地理学

root: 拉丁语 geographia，来自希腊语 geographia = ge「大地」+ graphein「书写、描画」。ge 的来源不确定，常视为前希腊语词；graphein 的词根清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the discipline to its object, its classroom, its branches, its business use, its spatial metaphor, its old descriptive sense, and finally to the shape of any situation.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从学科走到其对象、课堂、分支、商业用途、空间比喻、古老描述义，最后落到任何局势的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a world map spread open, its mountains, rivers and cities marked with symbols.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张铺开的世界地图，山脉、河流与城市用符号标出。

branches.en: WRITING AND STUDY: description of the earth grew into a disciplined study of it.
branches.cn: 书写与研究：对地球的描述发展为对它的系统研究。

branches.en: FIELD AND CLASSROOM: the same name covers the researcher's object and the pupil's lesson.
branches.cn: 研究对象与课堂：同一名称既指研究者的对象，也指学生的课程。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: human and physical branches divide the field without replacing its name.
branches.cn: 两半：人文与自然分支把领域分开，却未取代其名称。

branches.en: LOCATION AS VALUE: business and metaphor both read space as advantage and cost.
branches.cn: 位置即价值：商业与比喻都把空间读作优势与成本。

branches.en: ROOM AS TERRAIN: a situation acquires high ground, obstacles and distance.
branches.cn: 房间即地形：局势也有了高地、障碍与距离。

intro.en: Geography is built from two productive Greek elements, and its derivatives fill out a whole academic family.
intro.cn: geography 由两个多产的希腊语素构成，其派生词撑起整个学术词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin geographia is the borrowed form; Greek ge and graphein are the ultimate elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 geographia 是借入形式；希腊语 ge 与 graphein 是最终语素。

items.example: Ge- opens geography, geology and geometry.
items.exampleCN: ge- 出现在 geography、geology 与 geometry 开头。

items.example: Geography studies places and spatial patterns.
items.exampleCN: 地理学研究地方与空间格局。

items.meaningCN: 研究地方的人；地理学家
items.example: The geographer mapped the flood plain.
items.exampleCN: 地理学家绘制了洪泛区地图。

items.example: The two towns show a sharp geographic contrast.
items.exampleCN: 两座城镇呈现鲜明的地理对比。

items.meaningCN: 较完整的地理形容词形式
items.exampleCN: 该学会出版地理调查报告。
这个国家在地理上很孤立。

items.meaningCN: 研究地球岩石的学科；地质学
items.example: Geology studies the deep structure, not just the surface.
items.exampleCN: 地质学研究深部结构，而不只是地表。

items.meaningCN: 受位置塑造的政治；地缘政治
items.exampleCN: 地缘政治把边界当作地理。

definition_zh: 流感；流行性感冒
definition_en: an infectious illness with fever, coughing and aching, caught from a virus that spreads in seasons
core_image: 季节性来袭、烧得人浑身酸痛的传染病
scene: 班上一半同学咳嗽发烧，医生说这是换季时最容易传染的那种病。 He missed school for a week with the flu.
sceneCN: 这里 flu 是名词「流感」（第 1 个义项：由病毒引起的季节性传染病）；句意为他因流感一周没上学。

derivatives.zh: flu 的完整正式形式，义为「流行性感冒」
由 flu 加 like 构成，义为「类似流感症状的」
flu-like 的连写形式，义为「类似流感的」
由 fluor- 加后缀构成，与流感无关，义为「荧光的」（形近词）

senses.title: The infectious illness
senses.definition: a contagious illness with fever, cough and body aches caused by a virus
senses.definitionCN: 由病毒引起、伴发烧咳嗽与全身酸痛的传染病
senses.example: Half the class caught the flu.
senses.exampleCN: 班里一半人得了流感。
senses.why: The core image is an illness that sweeps through a community in one season.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个季节内扫过整个社区的疾病。

senses.title: Any similar seasonal viral illness
senses.definition: informally, any mild or similar viral illness of the season
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对类似季节性病毒疾病统称
senses.example: A stomach flu kept him at home.
senses.exampleCN: 一场肠胃感冒让他待在家。
senses.why: Because the name is short and familiar, people apply it to any passing seasonal bug.
senses.whyCN: 名字简短又常用，人们便把它泛用于任何来去匆匆的季节性疾病。

intro.en: Flu is a clipped form of influenza, an Italian word about influence.
intro.cn: flu 是 influenza 的截短形式，后者是源自意大利语、与「影响」有关的词。

items.en: Italian influenza meant influence; epidemics were blamed on astral or supernatural influence.
items.cn: 意大利语 influenza 意为影响；旧时人们把流行病归咎于星象或超自然的影响。

items.en: It goes back to Latin influere, to flow in, the picture of unseen forces flowing into people.
items.cn: 它源自拉丁语 influere「流入」，画面是无形之力流入人体。

items.en: The medical use passed through French influence before entering English in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 这一医学用法经法语 influence 传入，十八世纪进入英语。

items.en: English first used the full word influenza, then clipped it to flu by the mid-nineteenth century.
items.cn: 英语最初用全称 influenza，到十九世纪中叶截短为 flu。

items.en: Modern speech keeps flu as the everyday word and influenza for formal writing.
items.cn: 现代口语用 flu，正式文体则保留 influenza。

note.en: Flu has a few false friends that start with flu-.
note.cn: flu- 开头的词里有几个假朋友。

entries.definition: a chimney pipe for smoke
entries.definitionCN: 烟道；与 flu 同音异义

entries.definition: a liquid substance
entries.definitionCN: 液体；源自拉丁语 fluere「流动」，与 flu 词根不同但相关

entries.definition: speaking smoothly
entries.definitionCN: 流利的；同出拉丁语 fluere，与 flu 并非同词

entries.definition: a wind instrument
entries.definitionCN: 长笛；音近词源不同

entries.definition: a milder common viral illness
entries.definitionCN: 感冒；比流感轻的常见病毒病

entries.definition: the formal name of flu
entries.definitionCN: 流感全称；flu 的正式形式

entries.definition: a high body temperature
entries.definitionCN: 发烧；流感的主要症状

entries.definition: the germ that causes illness
entries.definitionCN: 病毒；引发流感的病原体

normalIntro.en: Five anchors for the word flu.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚定 flu 记忆的方法。

normal.en: flu is short for influenza.
normal.cn: flu 是 influenza 的缩略形式。

normal.en: flu sounds like flue, but flue is a chimney pipe.
normal.cn: flu 与 flue 同音，flue 是烟道。

normal.en: get a flu shot before flu season.
normal.cn: 流感季前打流感疫苗（flu shot）。

normal.en: flu and cold differ: flu brings fever and aches.
normal.cn: flu 与 cold 不同：flu 有发烧与酸痛。

normal.en: stomach flu is the informal name for a stomach virus.
normal.cn: stomach flu 是肠胃病毒的口语说法。

abstract.en: See a whole classroom coughing in the same week.
abstract.cn: 想象整间教室同一周齐声咳嗽。

abstract.en: Feel the deep ache that makes every muscle complain.
abstract.cn: 感受让全身肌肉叫苦的酸痛。

abstract.en: See a blanket, a hot cup, and a thermometer.
abstract.cn: 想象毯子、热饮与体温计。

examples.en: I had the flu all last week.
examples.cn: 我上周整个星期都在患流感。

examples.en: Grandma gets a flu shot every autumn.
examples.cn: 奶奶每年秋天都打流感疫苗。

examples.en: Flu season peaks in winter here.
examples.cn: 这里的流感季在冬天达到高峰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福流」——福气别流走，流感会传染

root: flu 是 influenza 的截短形式。influenza 经法语 influence 来自意大利语 influenza「影响」，追溯至拉丁语 influere「流入」——旧时认为流行病因星体影响「流入」人体。十九世纪起 flu 成为日常用词。

sensesIntro.en: Flu keeps one centre, the sweeping seasonal illness, with an informal stretch to similar bugs.
sensesIntro.cn: flu 始终以季节性传染病为中心，口语中可泛指类似疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a feverish illness sweeping a community in one season
core.cn: 核心意象：一季扫过社区的发烧传染病

branches.en: The illness itself
branches.cn: 疾病本身

branches.en: Informal use for similar illness
branches.cn: 对类似疾病的口语统称

branches.en: Everyday talk about seasonal sickness
branches.cn: 关于季节疾病的日常说法

branches.en: The formal-clipped pair flu / influenza
branches.cn: 正式与缩略的成对表达

branches.en: Loose naming of passing bugs
branches.cn: 对来去匆匆病症的宽泛称呼

intro.en: Flu is a clip, so the real word-building happens in influenza and the Latin flu- family.
intro.cn: flu 是截短词，真正的构词发生在 influenza 与拉丁语 flu- 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fluere means to flow; it builds fluent, fluid and influence, cousins that once shared flu's story.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fluere 意为流动，构成 fluent、fluid 与 influence，这些同族词曾与 flu 的故事交织。

items.meaning: a power flowing into people or things

items.meaningCN: 烟道（与 flu 同音异义）

items.meaning: a flowing in of people or money

definition_zh: 帆；航行；航行；轻快移动
definition_en: a large cloth that catches the wind; a journey by boat; to travel on water; to move smoothly and quickly
core_image: 一面被海风吹得鼓起来的白帆
scene: 他们黎明时起航。 They set sail at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 sail 是「航行、起航」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他们黎明时起航。

derivatives.zh: 水手；海员
航行；帆船运动
帆船

senses.title: The cloth that catches wind
senses.definition: a large piece of cloth fixed to a boat to catch the wind
senses.definitionCN: 固定在船上用来兜风的大块布
senses.example: The wind filled the sail.
senses.exampleCN: 风把帆吹得鼓起来。
senses.why: The core object is the cloth that drives a boat.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是推动船只的布。

senses.title: A journey by boat
senses.definition: a trip on water in a boat or ship
senses.definitionCN: 乘船在水上的行程
senses.example: The sail to the island takes two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 到岛上的航程需要两小时。
senses.why: The object becomes the journey it makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 物件变成它促成的航程。

senses.title: Travel on water
senses.definition: to travel on water using wind or an engine
senses.definitionCN: 利用风力或发动机在水上行驶
senses.example: They sail along the coast every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年夏天沿海岸航行。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action of travelling.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成航行的动作。

senses.title: Move smoothly
senses.definition: to move smoothly and confidently
senses.definitionCN: 平稳而自信地移动
senses.example: She sailed through the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻松通过了考试。
senses.why: Smooth travel becomes smooth success.
senses.whyCN: 平稳航行变成顺利成功。

intro.en: Sail comes from Old English segl, a word shared across Germanic languages.
intro.cn: sail 源自古英语 segl，这个词在日耳曼语中广泛存在。

items.en: Segl names the cloth that catches wind.
items.cn: segl 指兜风的布。

items.en: The word is related to cutting cloth.
items.cn: 这个词与裁剪布匹有关。

items.en: Sail names both the cloth and the journey.
items.cn: 中古英语中 sail 兼指帆与航程。

items.en: Sail becomes a verb for travelling on water.
items.cn: sail 成为表示水上航行的动词。

items.en: Sail also means to move smoothly.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sail 也指轻快移动。

note.en: Sail is the cloth or travel; sale is selling.
note.cn: sail 是帆或航行，sale 则是销售，两者同音。

entries.definition: the act of selling something

entries.definition: the earth in which plants grow

entries.definition: a small slow animal with a shell
entries.definitionCN: 蜗牛

entries.definition: a long journey by sea
entries.definitionCN: 航行；航海

entries.definitionCN: 滑行

normalIntro.en: Sail is the cloth, the journey, and the smooth movement of a boat.
normalIntro.cn: sail 既指帆，也指航程与船只的平稳移动。

normal.cn: 帆被强风撕破了。

normal.cn: 他们扬帆前往群岛。

normal.en: We sail along the river in summer.
normal.cn: 夏天我们沿河航行。

normal.en: The ship sailed into the harbour.
normal.cn: 船驶入港口。

normal.en: She sailed through the interview.
normal.cn: 她顺利通过了面试。

abstract.en: Picture a white sail filled by a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被强风鼓满的白帆。

abstract.cn: 想象小船平稳地划过蓝色水面。

examples.cn: 小船绕岛航行。

examples.cn: 我们在日出前起航。

examples.en: The team sailed through the first round.
examples.cn: 这支队伍轻松通过了第一轮。

sensesIntro.en: Sail means the cloth that catches wind, a boat journey, to travel on water, or to move smoothly.
sensesIntro.cn: sail 意为兜风的帆、乘船航程、在水上航行，或平稳移动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white sail filled by the wind.

definition_zh: 行动；行为；作用；（戏剧的）情节

senses.title: Doing something

senses.whyCN: action 是 act 的名词形式，所以指「做」这件事本身。

senses.title: A single deed
senses.definition: one thing that someone does

senses.whyCN: 把做的事数出来，就指一个具体的举动。

senses.title: The effect of a thing

definition_zh: 残忍的；残酷的；令人痛苦的
definition_en: causing pain or suffering on purpose; unkind and without pity
core_image: 明知对方会疼，仍然下重手
scene: 读童话时，我心疼那个被迫整夜干活的灰姑娘。 The cruel stepmother made her do all the housework.
sceneCN: 这里 cruel 是「残忍的」（第 1 个义项：故意让人受苦）；句意是残忍的继母让她做全部家务。

senses.title: Causing pain on purpose
senses.definition: hurting people or animals and enjoying it or not caring
senses.definitionCN: 伤害人或动物，且以此为乐或毫不在意
senses.example: It is cruel to laugh at a classmate's mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 嘲笑同学的错误是残忍的。
senses.why: The core image is a hand that presses even when the other side cries out, so willing harm is cruel.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是明知对方哭喊仍按下去的手，所以有意伤害就是 cruel。

senses.title: Harsh and hard to bear
senses.definition: causing suffering without intending any single person harm
senses.definitionCN: 带来苦难，但不针对某个具体的人
senses.example: The team lost the final in the last second, a cruel result.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在最后一秒输掉决赛，结果太残酷了。
senses.why: The same press can come from fate or weather, so outcomes and conditions wear the word too.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「按压」也可能来自命运或天气，所以结果与境况也可以用这个词。

intro.cn: cruel 经法语来自拉丁语，建立在「血」与「心」之上。

items.cn: 古法语将其变为 cruel，意为铁石心肠的。

items.en: English borrowed cruel in the thirteenth century for merciless people.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 cruel，形容无情的人。

items.en: Its noun cruelty named both the feeling and the acts.
items.cn: 名词 cruelty 既指这种心态，也指具体行为。

items.en: Cruel now covers people, jokes, weather and fate.
items.cn: 如今 cruel 可形容人、玩笑、天气与命运。

note.cn: 这些词属于 cruel 词族，或指严酷的行为。

senses.title: Natural from the start
senses.definition: having a quality from birth rather than learning it
senses.definitionCN: 从出生起就具备某种特质，而非后天学来
senses.example: He is a born teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个天生的老师。
senses.why: If a quality is present at birth, it seems to come with the person, so born came to mean natural.
senses.whyCN: 一种特质若在出生时就有，看上去就是随人而来的，于是 born 引申为「天生的」。

senses.title: Beginning to exist
senses.definition: used of an idea, group or situation that starts to exist
senses.definitionCN: 用于开始出现的想法、群体或局面
senses.example: The idea was born in a late-night talk.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法诞生于一次深夜长谈。
senses.why: New ideas are pictured as newborns: they appear at a moment, small and needing care.
senses.whyCN: 新想法被比作新生儿：在某一刻出现，幼小且需要照料。

intro.en: Born is the old past participle of the verb bear, and its meaning has spread from babies to ideas.
intro.cn: born 是动词 bear 的古老过去分词，它的意思从婴儿扩展到想法。

items.en: Old English boren was the past participle of beran, meaning to carry or give birth.
items.cn: 古英语 boren 是 beran 的过去分词，意为承载或生育。

items.en: The verb beran meant to carry, and a child born is a child carried into the world.
items.cn: 动词 beran 意为承载，出生的孩子就是被带到世上的孩子。

items.en: German gebären and Dutch baren belong to the same family of birth words.
items.cn: 德语 gebären 与荷兰语 baren 属于同一个表示生育的词族。

items.en: English split the two forms: born for birth, borne for carrying other things.
items.cn: 英语把两个形式分了工：born 用于出生，borne 用于承载其他事物。

items.en: Today born also describes natural qualities and the starting of ideas and movements.
items.cn: 今天 born 也形容天生的特质，以及想法与运动的产生。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape or sound; the near-meaning group collects words about birth and nature.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音接近的词；近义组收与出生、天性有关的词。

entries.definition: The other past participle of bear, used for carrying and enduring.
entries.definitionCN: bear 的另一个过去分词，用于「承载、忍受」等义。

entries.definition: The past tense of bear, and also a verb meaning to drill or to weary.
entries.definitionCN: bear 的过去式，也是表示「钻孔、使厌烦」的动词。

entries.definition: The seeds of grain plants, or maize.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「谷物；玉米」，读音与 born 接近。

entries.definition: The moment when a baby is born.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出生」，指婴儿降生的时刻。

entries.definition: Present from birth rather than learned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「天生的；固有的」，对应 born 的天性义。

entries.definition: Belonging to a place by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本地的；与生俱来的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English boren was the past participle of beran, meaning to carry or give birth.
normal.cn: 古英语 boren 是 beran 的过去分词，意为承载或生育。

normal.en: A child born is a child carried into the world, which is the picture inside the word.
normal.cn: 出生的孩子就是被带到世上的孩子，这是这个词里的画面。

normal.en: English keeps born for birth and borne for carrying other things.
normal.cn: 英语让 born 专管出生，让 borne 管承载其他事物。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with in, with, to and of.
normal.cn: 它常与 in、with、to、of 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-r-n; the or sounds like the o in more.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-r-n，中间的 or 读得像 more 里的 o。

abstract.en: Hear the first cry in a delivery room: that moment is born.
abstract.cn: 想象产房里传来的第一声啼哭：那一刻就是 born。

abstract.en: Let a new idea appear just as suddenly, and the word still fits.
abstract.cn: 让一个新想法同样突然地出现，这个词仍然适用。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the first cry bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那第一声啼哭把意思带回来。

examples.en: She was born in a small village.
examples.cn: 她出生在一个小村庄。

examples.en: He is a born teacher.
examples.cn: 他是个天生的老师。

examples.en: The idea was born in a late-night talk.
examples.cn: 这个想法诞生于一次深夜长谈。

root: born 是古英语 boren，即动词 beran（承载、生育）的过去分词；德语 gebären 与荷兰语 baren 同属一个表示生育的词族。英语把两个过去分词分了工：born 用于出生，borne 用于承载其他事物。由「被带到世上」的画面，born 又引申为「天生的」，以及想法、群体、运动的「产生」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of born rest on one picture: a child carried into the world, and then anything that appears at a starting moment.
sensesIntro.cn: born 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：一个被带到世上的孩子，以及任何在一个开端时刻出现的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first cry in a delivery room
core.cn: 核心意象：产房里的第一声啼哭

branches.en: THE BIRTH: coming out of the mother's body is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 出生线：从母体中出来是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE NATURE: a quality present at birth is called born.
branches.cn: 天性线：出生时就有的特质被称作 born。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: ideas and groups are pictured as newborns too.
branches.cn: 起源线：想法与群体也被比作新生儿。

branches.en: THE START: birth and inborn quality share the same beginning.
branches.cn: 开端线：出生与天生的特质共享同一个开端。

branches.en: THE APPEARING: a baby and a new idea both come into being.
branches.cn: 出现线：婴儿与新想法都是「开始存在」。

intro.en: Born is a past participle used as an adjective, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: born 是作形容词用的过去分词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin natus and nasci are recorded words for born and to be born; they are parallels, not the source of born.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 natus 与 nasci 分别是有记录的「出生的」与「出生」，它们是平行词，不是 born 的来源。

items.example: Boren is the recorded Old English form.
items.exampleCN: boren 是有记录的古英语形式。

definition_zh: 文化；文明；培养；种植
definition_en: the ideas, customs and art of a group of people; the growing of plants or cells
core_image: 一群人共同浇灌出来的一片精神花园
scene: 美术课上，老师给我们看了很多外国节日和传统服饰的图片。 Learning about another country's culture makes the world feel smaller.
sceneCN: 这里 culture 是「文化」（第 1 个义项：一群人共同的思想、习俗与艺术）；句意是了解别国的文化会让世界显得更小、更亲近。

derivatives.zh: 由 culture 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「文化的」
由 cultural 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在文化上」
由拉丁词根 agri（田地）加 culture 构成，义为「农业」
由拉丁词根 cult-（耕种）构成，义为「耕作；培养」

senses.title: The customs and art of a group of people
senses.titleCN: 一群人的文化、习俗与艺术
senses.definition: the ideas, beliefs, music, food and ways of living shared by a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体共同拥有的想法、信仰、音乐、饮食和生活方式
senses.example: Our class made a poster about food culture in different countries.
senses.exampleCN: 我们班做了一张关于各国饮食文化的海报。
senses.why: A garden grows many plants together; a people grows many shared habits together, so shared living became a garden of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 花园里种着许多植物，一个民族也种出许多共同的习惯，所以共同的活法就像一座心灵花园，这个词便由此长出。

senses.title: Art, music and literature
senses.definition: activities and interests such as music, art, theatre and literature
senses.definitionCN: 音乐、艺术、戏剧、文学之类的活动和兴趣
senses.example: The city offers young people lots of culture, from museums to concerts.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市为年轻人提供了很多文化熏陶，从博物馆到音乐会。
senses.why: Museums and concerts are the most polished flowers in the shared garden, so the word pointed at high art.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆和音乐会是共同花园里最精心培育的花朵，于是这个词便指向高雅艺术。

senses.title: Growing plants or cells
senses.definition: the practice of growing plants, or keeping cells or bacteria alive for study
senses.definitionCN: 种植植物，或为研究而培养细胞、细菌
senses.example: The culture of rice needs warm weather and plenty of water.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻的种植需要温暖的天气和充足的水。
senses.why: The Latin root meant tilling the soil, so growing plants kept the oldest meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本义是耕作土地，所以「种植物」保留了这个词最古老的意思。

intro.en: Culture grows from a Latin word for working the soil.
intro.cn: culture 从一个表示耕作土地的拉丁词生长而来。

items.en: The verb colere meant to till, to dwell, and to worship; cultura was the noun for tilling the land.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 colere 意为耕作、居住、崇敬；cultura 是耕地的名词。

items.en: Scholars used cultura to describe tilling the mind, such as cultura animi, the care of the soul.
items.cn: 中世纪学者用 cultura 比喻耕耘心灵，如 cultura animi（心灵的培育）。

items.en: Old French carried couture and culture into learned writing, still close to cultivation.
items.cn: 古法语把 couture、culture 带进书面语，意思仍接近「培育」。

items.en: English took culture in the fifteenth century, first for the growing of crops.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 culture，最初指庄稼的种植。

items.en: By the nineteenth century it covered art and shared ways of life, and later science kept it for growing cells.
items.cn: 到十九世纪它已涵盖艺术和共同的生活方式；后来科学界又用它指培养细胞。

note.en: These words share the Latin root colere or describe the shared life of a people.
note.cn: 这些词与拉丁词根 colere 同源，或同样描述一个群体的共同生活。

normalIntro.cn: 用「耕地」的画面和 culture 词族来记住这个词。

normal.cn: cult- 来自拉丁语 colere，耕作土地。

normal.cn: agri-（田地）+ culture ＝ agriculture（农业）。

normal.en: cultural is the adjective: cultural events, cultural differences.
normal.cn: 形容词是 cultural：cultural events（文化活动）。

normal.cn: cultivate 保留了耕地义：cultivate the land（耕田）、cultivate a hobby（培养爱好）。

abstract.en: Picture a field where every plant is a shared habit of a people.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田地，每一棵植物都是一个群体的共同习惯。

abstract.en: Hear museum halls as greenhouses where art flowers are raised.
abstract.cn: 把博物馆大厅想象成培育艺术花朵的温室。

abstract.en: Feel the patience of a farmer; a culture is grown slowly, year by year.
abstract.cn: 体会农夫的耐心；文化是一年一年慢慢种出来的。

examples.en: We learned about the culture of ancient Egypt in history class.
examples.cn: 历史课上我们了解了古埃及的文化。

examples.en: Every country has its own culture and festivals.
examples.cn: 每个国家都有自己的文化和节日。

examples.en: Farmers care for the culture of vegetables from spring to autumn.
examples.cn: 从春天到秋天，农民悉心照料蔬菜的种植。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡尺」——用同一把卡尺量出来的习惯，就是一个群体的「文化」

sensesIntro.en: The word grows from farming the land to tending art and shared habits.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从耕种土地，扩展到培育艺术和群体的共同习惯。

intro.cn: culture 建立在一个表示耕作与照料的拉丁词根上。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cult- 意为耕作或照料。

definition_zh: 考试；测验（examination 的缩略形式）
definition_en: a formal test of knowledge, short for examination
core_image: 课桌上倒扣的考卷：铃声一响才能翻开
scene: 监考老师把试卷正面朝下放到每张课桌上。 I stayed up late to prepare for the maths exam.
sceneCN: 这里 exam 是「考试」（第 1 个义项：正式的知识测验）；句意是我熬夜备考数学考试。

derivatives.zh: 完整正式形式，义为「考试；检查」
同根动词，义为「检查；测验」
由 examine 加 -er 构成，义为「主考官；检查者」

senses.title: A formal test of knowledge
senses.definition: an official test that shows how much a student has learned
senses.definitionCN: 检验学生学习程度的正式测验
senses.example: The history exam has two parts: writing and speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 历史考试有两部分：笔试和口试。
senses.why: The root examine means to weigh a thing carefully, so an exam weighs what a student knows.
senses.whyCN: 词根 examine 意为仔细称量，考试便是称量学生所知。

senses.title: A close inspection or medical check
senses.definition: a careful look at something or someone, especially a medical one
senses.definitionCN: 对事物或人的仔细查看，尤指医疗检查
senses.example: The doctor gave the patient a quick exam.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给病人做了快速检查。
senses.why: Weighing a patient's health reuses the same careful-measuring picture.
senses.whyCN: 称量病人的健康，复用同一「细量」画面。

intro.en: Exam is the short form of examination, which comes from Latin examinare, to weigh or test. A good exam really is a set of scales for learning.
intro.cn: exam 是 examination 的缩略形式，后者源自拉丁语 examinare「称量、测验」。考试就是学习的秤。

items.en: Latin exigere meant to weigh out or drive out, the base of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 exigere 意为称量完、驱出，是词族的基础。

items.en: Examinare meant to weigh or test a thing or a person.
items.cn: examinare 意为称量或测验某物某人。

items.en: English borrowed examination in the fourteenth century for careful testing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 examination，指仔细的检验。

items.en: Schools adopted the word for formal tests of knowledge.
items.cn: 学校将该词用于正式的知识测验。

items.en: The clipped form exam became general speech by the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 缩略形式 exam 到十九世纪成为通用口语。

note.en: The first group collects the examin- family; the second collects near meanings about tests.
note.cn: 第一组收集 examin- 词族；第二组收集与「测验」相关的近义词。

entries.definitionCN: 考试（完整形式）。正式书面用语。

entries.definition: the person who sets or marks an exam

entries.definition: an official judgment of ability or progress
entries.definitionCN: 评估。正式的判定与评价。

normal.en: Take an exam, pass or fail: the verbs pair up neatly.
normal.cn: take an exam 参加考试；pass／fail 一过一挂。

normal.en: Final exam and midterm exam mark the two ends of a term.

abstract.en: Picture upside-down papers on desks waiting for the bell.
abstract.cn: 画面：课桌上倒扣的考卷静待铃声。

abstract.en: Feel a hand placing weights on a scale until it balances.
abstract.cn: 动作：往秤上加砝码直到平衡。

abstract.en: Hear the long silence of a room where everyone is thinking.
abstract.cn: 听觉：满室思考的长久安静。

examples.en: Our English exam is next Friday morning.
examples.cn: 我们的英语考试在下周五上午。

examples.en: She passed all her exams with high marks.
examples.cn: 她所有考试都以高分通过。

examples.en: The school nurse gave everyone an eye exam.
examples.cn: 校医给每个人做了视力检查。

sensesIntro.en: Exam weighs what you know and how healthy you are: two scales, one careful habit of measuring.
sensesIntro.cn: exam 既称量所学，也称量健康：两杆秤，同一种细量的习惯。

items.exampleCN: 小测验抽样检验你的知识。

definition_zh: 必须；一定；必需品
definition_en: used to say that something is necessary or almost certainly true; as a noun, something that cannot be left out
core_image: 一道关着的闸门，旁边只留一条必须走过去的通道
scene: 地铁入口处，安检员抬手示意乘客停下，把背包放上检查带。 You must put your bag on the belt before you walk through.
sceneCN: 这里是「必须、有义务」（第 1 个义项：被要求做某事）；句意为过闸之前你得出示并放下背包接受检查。图中可辨识物件：闸门、检查带、背包。

collocations.zh: 一定做过（对过去的推测）

derivatives.zh: 由 must 与 have 复合，义为「必备品」
由 must 与 see 复合，义为「必看之物」

senses.title: To be obliged to do something
senses.definition: used to say that a person is obliged or forced to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人有义务或不得不做某事
senses.example: You must show your ticket at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须在门口出示车票。
senses.why: Old English moste was the past of motan and often meant had to; the old sense of permission narrowed into a demand, so the word now states an obligation rather than an option.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 moste 是 motan 的过去式，常表示「当时不得不」；原先的许可义收窄成强制义，所以这个词现在陈述的是义务，而不是选项。

senses.title: To be very likely true
senses.definition: used to say that something is almost certainly true, judging from the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 依据证据判断某事几乎肯定成立
senses.example: The lights are off; they must have gone home.
senses.exampleCN: 灯都灭了，他们一定已经回家了。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, the mind treats the conclusion as unavoidable too, so the force of obligation slides into inference about what has to be the case.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事无法回避，人心也会把相应结论看成躲不开的，于是义务的力量滑向「情况必然如此」的推断。

senses.title: Something that cannot be left out
senses.definition: a thing that is absolutely necessary or strongly recommended
senses.definitionCN: 绝对必要或强烈建议不可省略的事物
senses.example: A torch is a must when you camp in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 在山里露营，手电是必备的。
senses.why: The noun keeps the force of the modal: anything called a must is treated as something one cannot skip, which is how a demand turns into an object on a packing list.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法保留了情态动词的力量：被称作 a must 的东西，被当成不能跳过的事物，于是一项要求就变成了清单上的一个物件。

intro.en: Must grew out of an Old English verb for being able or allowed; its past tense took over the present meaning of obligation.
intro.cn: must 源自古英语中表示「能够、被允许」的动词，它的过去式后来接管了现在时的义务义。

items.en: The verb reconstructed as motan is generally thought to have meant to have room or power to do something.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 motan 意为「有做某事的余地或力量」。

items.en: Motan meant to be able or to be permitted, and its past tense moste often carried the practical sense of having to.
items.cn: motan 意为能够或被允许，其过去式 moste 常带有「只好、不得不」的实感。

items.en: Moste spread into more contexts than the old present form, and speakers began to use it for present obligations.
items.cn: moste 的使用范围超过了旧的现在式，说话人开始用它表达当下的义务。

items.en: Must settled as an unchanging present form, took a contracted negative mustn't, and lost the old infinitive and participle.
items.cn: must 固定为没有词形变化的现在式，出现缩略否定 mustn't，旧的动词不定式和分词形式逐渐消失。

items.en: Modern English adds the inference use and the countable noun a must, plus compounds such as must-have and must-see.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了推测用法和可数名词 a must，还产生 must-have、must-see 这类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the negative contraction and three words that only resemble must in spelling; the near-meaning group holds other ways of expressing obligation.
note.cn: 形近组收 must 的否定缩略式，以及三个只是拼写相似、来源不同的词；近义组收其他表示义务的说法。

entries.definition: The contracted negative of must, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: must 的否定缩略形式，口语中常见。

entries.definition: To gather people or courage for a purpose; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 召集人员或鼓起勇气；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A yellow sharp condiment made from seeds; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 用种子制成的黄色辛辣调味酱；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Smelling damp and stale, as an old room does; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 有潮湿霉味的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Expresses external obligation like must, but uses do in questions and negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 与 must 一样表示外在义务，但疑问和否定要借助 do。

entries.definition: Gives advice or a mild duty rather than a firm demand.
entries.definitionCN: 给出建议或轻微责任，语气不如 must 强硬。

entries.definition: States a duty seen as right, often in careful or written English.
entries.definitionCN: 表示按道理应尽的责任，多见于正式或书面英语。

entries.definition: Names a requirement, usually followed by to before a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指出一项需求，动词前通常带 to。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic modal that drifted from permission to obligation, with a negative contraction and two modern compounds around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语情态动词，从许可漂移到义务，周围还有一个否定缩略式和两个现代复合词。

normal.en: Old English motan meant to be able or allowed, and its past moste meant had to; must is that past form grown into a present.
normal.cn: 古英语 motan 意为能够、被允许，其过去式 moste 意为不得不；must 就是这个过去式长成了现在式。

normal.en: Must is followed by the bare verb: must go, never must to go.
normal.cn: must 后面直接跟动词原形：说 must go，不说 must to go。

normal.en: Mustn't forbids, while can't denies a guess: you mustn't smoke here, but he can't be at home.
normal.cn: mustn't 表示禁止，can't 才用来否定推测：此处不许吸烟，而「他不可能在家」要用 can't。

normal.en: Must have done looks back at a past certainty, which is why the perfect follows must, not the past tense.
normal.cn: must have done 回看一件过去确定的事，所以 must 后面接完成式，而不是过去式。

normal.en: The noun a must copies the modal's force: a must-have item is one you cannot leave out.
normal.cn: 名词 a must 沿用了情态动词的力量：a must-have item 就是不能省略的东西。

abstract.en: A gate that only opens one way turns an old permission word into a word of compulsion.
abstract.cn: 一道只能单向打开的闸门，把旧的许可词变成了强制词。

abstract.en: When no other route exists, a demand and a certainty feel like the same pressure.
abstract.cn: 当没有别的路可走，一项要求和一种确定感会显得是同一种压力。

abstract.en: Every packing list is a small museum of things someone decided they could not do without.
abstract.cn: 每一张行李清单，都是「有人认定不能没有」的小小陈列馆。

examples.en: Visitors must sign in at the front desk.
examples.cn: 访客必须在前台登记。

examples.en: She must have missed the last bus.
examples.cn: 她一定是错过了末班车。

examples.en: A good pair of gloves is a must in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天一副好手套是必备的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马斯特」——教练马斯特站在跑道边说：必须跑完这一圈；must 就是必须。

root: 古英语 motan（能够、被允许），过去式 moste 逐渐固定为 must；一般认为与德语 müssen 同出原始日耳曼语 motan，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unavoidable demand; from it grow the inference about what must be true and the noun for a thing one cannot leave out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是躲不开的要求；由此长出「情况必然如此」的推断，以及指「不能省略之物」的名词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate with only one open passage, where stopping is not an option.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只留一条通道的闸门，停下不在选项之内。

branches.en: a guard raising a hand at the entrance
branches.cn: 入口处抬手示意的安检员

branches.en: a bag opened before the belt
branches.cn: 放上检查带之前的背包

branches.en: a dark window and a guess about who is inside
branches.cn: 暗着的窗和关于里面是谁的猜测

branches.en: a note that reads had to, written as must
branches.cn: 把「不得不」写成 must 的便条

branches.en: a torch placed first in the camp bag
branches.cn: 露营包里最先放手电的位置

intro.en: The word rests on one Old English modal, its past form, a negative clitic, and two modern compounds that turn the modal into a noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的一个情态动词、它的过去式、一个否定附着成分，以及两个把情态动词变成名词的现代复合词支撑。

latinIntro.en: Must belongs to the Germanic modals, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
latinIntro.cn: must 属于日耳曼语情态动词，因此没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to be able, to be permitted
was able, was allowed, had to

definition_zh: 杀死；弄死；毁掉；消磨（时间）；使痛苦
definition_en: to cause the death of a living thing, and by extension to end, ruin, or use up something such as time or a feeling
core_image: 一击落下，原本还在动的东西彻底静止
scene: 巷子里那只被撞伤的猫躺在墙根，谁都下不了手。 No one in the yard had the heart to kill the injured bird, so they called a vet instead.
sceneCN: 这里 kill 是「杀死、弄死」（第 1 个义项：使活物死亡），句意是院里没人忍心弄死那只受伤的小鸟，于是打电话叫了兽医。背景是墙根、受伤的小动物和一部电话。

collocations.phrase: kill two birds with one stone

derivatives.zh: kill 加 -er 构成，指杀人者或致命之物
kill 加 -ing 构成，指杀害行为，口语中也指「赚了一大笔」
kill 与 joy 合成的复合词，指扫兴的人
over 与 kill 合成，原指火力过剩，今指做得过头

senses.title: To take the life of a living thing
senses.definition: to cause the death of a person, animal, or plant
senses.definitionCN: 使某人、某动物或某植物死亡
senses.example: The frost killed the young shoots overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻一夜之间冻死了嫩芽。
senses.why: The oldest sense rests on a simple physical picture: a blow that ends all movement.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项基于一个简单的画面：一击下去，一切动静都停止了。

senses.title: To end something as if by a blow
senses.definition: to destroy or bring an end to something non-living, such as a plan or a hope
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、希望等非生物的事物毁灭或终止
senses.example: One careless remark killed the whole idea.
senses.exampleCN: 一句随口的话就把整个想法扼杀了。
senses.why: Because the literal act ends life, the word readily transfers to anything that stops growing.
senses.whyCN: 因为本义是终止生命，这个词很自然就挪用到任何停止生长的事物上。

senses.title: To use up time
senses.definition: to pass time while waiting, especially in a way that fills the empty hours
senses.definitionCN: 在等待时把空闲的时间打发过去
senses.example: We killed an hour at the station by counting trains.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站数着列车，消磨了一个小时。
senses.why: Empty time feels like something to be got rid of, so the word for ending life serves for ending boredom.
senses.whyCN: 空白的时间像是要处理掉的东西，于是表示结束生命的词也用来结束无聊。

senses.title: To cause great pain
senses.definition: to hurt someone badly, especially through emotion rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 多指在情感上把人伤害得极重，而非用武力
senses.example: His silence killed me more than any shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 他的沉默比任何喊叫都更让我难受。
senses.why: When pain is extreme it is described as the worst the body can bear, so the strongest word for ending is borrowed for suffering.
senses.whyCN: 痛苦到了极点就被说成身体能承受的极限，于是表示终结的最强词被借来表示难受。

senses.title: To stop a machine or engine
senses.definition: to switch off an engine or a device
senses.definitionCN: 把发动机或设备关掉
senses.example: Kill the engine before you check the oil.
senses.exampleCN: 检查机油之前先熄火。
senses.why: An engine that stops is dead in miniature, so drivers say they kill it.
senses.whyCN: 停下来的发动机就像小规模地死掉，所以司机说把它关掉。

senses.title: To defeat completely
senses.definition: to beat an opponent so thoroughly that the contest is over
senses.definitionCN: 把对手打败到比赛立刻失去悬念
senses.example: The away team killed the game in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 客队在上半场就让比赛失去悬念。
senses.why: In sport, ending the contest feels like killing its chances, so the word names total dominance.
senses.whyCN: 在体育里，终结比赛的悬念就像把机会杀掉，于是这个词用来指完全的压制。

senses.title: To cancel or remove a story
senses.definition: to drop a piece of news or a planned piece of work before it appears
senses.definitionCN: 在新闻或稿件发表之前把它撤掉不用
senses.example: The editor killed the interview at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑在最后一刻把访谈稿撤了下来。
senses.why: In newsrooms the act of striking a story from the page was called killing it, and the usage stayed.
senses.whyCN: 在编辑部里把稿子从版面上划掉被称作杀掉稿件，这种说法沿用至今。

senses.title: To process a drug or germ
senses.definition: to destroy germs, or to weaken a drug so that it can no longer be active
senses.definitionCN: 消灭细菌，或使药物失去活性
senses.example: Boiling the water kills most of the bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 把水烧开能杀死大部分细菌。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the original image: a living agent is made inoperative.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了原本的画面：让活的因子失去作用。

senses.title: The animal killed in hunting
senses.definition: an animal that has been hunted and killed, especially in sport
senses.definitionCN: 狩猎中打到的猎物，尤指运动狩猎所得
senses.example: The hounds brought down a fine kill.
senses.exampleCN: 猎犬包抄下一头不错的猎物。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun by naming the result of its own action, a common path in English.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接名词化，指自己行为的结果，这是英语里常见的一条路。

intro.en: Kill is a Middle English word whose roots are uncertain; it is not related to Latin occidere, and the common guess about a Latin origin has no solid support.
intro.cn: kill 是中古英语词，词根来源不确定；它与拉丁语 occidere 无关，常见的那种拉丁来源猜测缺乏可靠证据。

items.en: The verb appears as killen in Middle English, first in northern texts.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中写作 killen，最早见于北部地区的文本。

items.en: Its earliest recorded use concerns striking or beating, with dying as a result.
items.cn: 它最早的记录用法是打、击，结果是死亡。

items.en: No agreed source has been found; a link with Old English cwellan is often suggested but not proved.
items.cn: 至今未找到公认的来源；常有人提出与古英语 cwellan 有关，但未得到证实。

items.en: The plain sense ending life is fixed in English from the sixteenth century onwards.
items.cn: 表示结束生命的直白义项从十六世纪起在英语中固定下来。

items.en: The extended senses of ruining a plan, passing time, and switching off a machine all grow from that plain sense.
items.cn: 毁掉计划、打发时间、关掉机器等引申义都从这一直白义项生长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that are spelled or sounded close to kill; the near-meaning group holds stronger and weaker ways of saying the same act.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音接近 kill 的词；近义组收同一行为的更重与更轻的说法。

entries.definition: The same ending with a different first letter, naming raised ground.
entries.definitionCN: 只差首字母的拼写近邻，指小山，词源与 kill 无关。

entries.definition: A silent letter makes kiln look like kill plus n, but it is a baking oven.
entries.definitionCN: 多一个不发音的字母，看起来像 kill 加 n，其实指烧窑。

entries.definition: One letter away, naming the pleated Scottish skirt.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指苏格兰褶裙。

entries.definition: A spelling in some old glossaries for a small stream, unrelated and obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 某个旧词表里的拼写，指小溪，与 kill 无关且已废弃。

entries.definition: To kill a person unlawfully and with intent.
entries.definitionCN: 指非法且有预谋地杀人，是法律用语。

entries.definition: To kill, used mostly of heroes and dragons in old stories.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死，多用于旧故事里的英雄与恶龙。

entries.definition: To kill a sick animal humanely.
entries.definitionCN: 指为结束痛苦而人道地杀死患病动物。

entries.definition: To injure without causing death.
entries.definitionCN: 指伤害而未致死，与 kill 的结果相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the plain act to the many things people say they kill besides creatures.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从最直白的动作出发，走到人们说被 kill 掉的、动物以外的种种东西。

normal.en: Kill takes -s, -ed, and -ing without any stem change.
normal.cn: kill 变三单、过去式、现在分词都不改词干。

normal.en: Kill time literally makes the clock feel dead.
normal.cn: kill time 就是把钟面上的时间弄死。

normal.en: The -er ending gives killer, the one who does it.
normal.cn: 加 -er 得到 killer，指做这件事的人。

normal.en: One shot, two birds: the proverb packs the whole word.
normal.cn: 一箭双雕的谚语把这个词的全部用法都装了进去。

normal.en: Kill the engine is the everyday mechanical sense.
normal.cn: kill the engine 是日常里的机械用法。

abstract.en: A struck match: the tiny flame goes out in a blink, and the smallest moment of death is the word itself.
abstract.cn: 划着又熄灭的火柴：小火苗一眨眼就没，死亡最小的那一瞬就是这个词。

abstract.en: An empty afternoon is a stretch of clock to be used up, so people speak of killing it.
abstract.cn: 空荡荡的下午是一段等着被用完的时钟，所以人们说要 killing it。

abstract.en: A word killed in an editor's room never reaches print, yet it still dies.
abstract.cn: 被编辑在屋里撤掉的稿子从没见报，可它照样死过一次。

examples.en: Too much rain can kill a young crop.
examples.cn: 雨水太多会把幼苗淹死。

examples.en: She killed the lights before leaving the studio.
examples.cn: 她离开工作室前把灯关了。

examples.en: We killed the whole afternoon arguing about a name.
examples.cn: 我们为一个名字争了整个下午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剋」——剋死，古书里的字正好握住了这个词的狠劲

root: 中古英语 killen，最早记录的是「打、击」而致死；来源不确定，或有与古英语 cwellan（杀）相关的可能，但未证实；十六世纪起固定为「结束生命」，并引申出毁掉、消磨、关掉等义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses: the plain act of ending life, then the ending of plans, hours, pain, engines, contests, stories, and germs, and finally the hunted animal itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项：先是结束生命的直白动作，接着是结束计划、时间、痛苦、机器、悬念、稿件与细菌，最后是以动词结果命名的猎物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one blow, and the thing that was moving stops for good.
core.cn: 核心意象：一击落下，原本还在动的东西彻底停住。

branches.en: THE BLOW LINE: a strike ends a living thing, from animals to germs.
branches.cn: 打击这条线：一击结束一个活物，从动物到细菌。

branches.en: THE ENDING LINE: anything that stops growing is spoken of as killed, even hope or a story.
branches.cn: 终结这条线：任何停止生长的东西都被说成被杀，包括希望和稿子。

branches.en: THE CLOCK LINE: empty time is used up as if it were alive.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：空白的时间像活物一样被用掉。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE LINE: extreme pain and total defeat both borrow the strongest word.
branches.cn: 压力这条线：极度的痛和彻底的胜都借用这个最重的词。

branches.en: THE SWITCH LINE: an engine that stops is a small death.
branches.cn: 开关这条线：停下来的发动机就是一次小死亡。

intro.en: Kill is a short native verb that builds mostly by compounding, so the items below are the small set of words English made from it.
intro.cn: kill 是一个短小的本土动词，主要靠合成造词，下面的条目是英语由它构成的少数词。

latinIntro.en: Kill has no Latin ancestry, so the Latin-looking forms below are offered only as contrasts to the real word family.
latinIntro.cn: kill 没有拉丁血统，下面这些看似拉丁的形式只是与真实词族的对照。

items.example: One fall killed the old tree.
items.exampleCN: 一次倒伏弄死了那棵老树。

items.example: The killing of the wolf ended the attacks.
items.exampleCN: 打死那只狼之后袭击就停了。

items.meaning: a person or thing that kills
items.example: Heart disease is a leading killer.
The killjoy closed the party early.
items.exampleCN: 那个扫兴的人早早结束了聚会。

items.example: Two guards for one door is overkill.
items.exampleCN: 一扇门配两个守卫实在过头。
乌鸦聚在被撞死的动物上方。
它把 kill 变成 killer。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「打倒、杀死」，与 kill 只是意义相近，并非同源
拉丁语「砍、击倒」，为拉丁系杀伐词的根，与 kill 无词源关系

definition_zh: 幸运地；幸好；侥幸
definition_en: by good luck; luckily
core_image: 掉落的杯子刚好落进接住的网：危险擦身而过
scene: 爬山时天下起大雨，同学们正好走到半山腰的亭子里避雨。 Fortunately, they had reached the shelter just before the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 fortunately 是「幸好」的意思（第 1 个义项：因运气好而避免坏事）；他们恰好赶在大雨前到了亭子。

derivatives.zh: fortunately 的形容词形式，义为「幸运的；侥幸的」
同根名词，义为「运气；财富；命运」
un- + fortunately，义为「不幸地；遗憾地」
mis- + fortune，义为「不幸；灾祸」

senses.title: By good luck
senses.definition: happening because of good luck, often preventing something bad
senses.definitionCN: 因运气好而发生，常指躲过了坏事。
senses.example: Fortunately, the fire was put out quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 幸好大火很快被扑灭了。
senses.why: The word comes from fortune, the turning wheel of luck, plus the adverb ending.
senses.whyCN: 该词来自 fortune（命运之轮）加副词后缀，核心是「运气转动」的意象。

senses.title: As luck would have it (sentence adverb)
senses.titleCN: 作为评注：幸好（句子副词）
senses.definition: used to comment on a whole sentence, showing relief
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首评注整句，表达「万幸、松了口气」的态度。
senses.example: Fortunately, nobody was in the building when it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 幸好楼塌的时候楼里没人。
senses.why: The adverb floats to the front of the sentence to judge the whole event.
senses.whyCN: 副词移到句首，对整个事件作出评判。

intro.en: Fortunately traces back to the Roman goddess of luck, Fortuna, through Latin and Old French.
intro.cn: fortunately 可追溯到罗马命运女神 Fortuna，经拉丁语和古法语传入英语。

items.en: Fortuna was the goddess of chance, and fors meant luck or chance.
items.cn: Fortuna 是掌管机运的女神，fors 意为「运气、机缘」。

items.en: Fortunatus meant made happy by luck, the base of fortunate.
items.cn: fortunatus 意为「被运气眷顾的」，是 fortunate 的基础。

items.en: The word entered Old French as fortune, covering luck and wealth.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语写作 fortune，兼指运气与财富。

items.en: English borrowed fortune and built fortunate, then added -ly for the adverb.
items.cn: 英语借入 fortune，派生 fortunate，再加 -ly 构成副词。

items.en: The sentence-initial use commenting on lucky outcomes became standard.
items.cn: 置于句首、对幸运结果作总评的用法成为标准。

note.en: Words shaped like fortunately and words about luck and chance.
note.cn: 与 fortunately 形近的词，以及表示运气、机缘的词。

entries.definition: by bad luck; the negative twin of fortunately
entries.definitionCN: 不幸地；fortunately 的否定孪生词。

entries.definition: a strong building for defence; shares letters but not the luck meaning
entries.definitionCN: 堡垒；与 fortunately 字母相近，但词义与运气无关。

entries.definition: giving ease; contains com- + fort, a different root
entries.definitionCN: 舒适的；含 com- + fort 词根，与幸运词源不同。

entries.definition: by good luck; the everyday synonym
entries.definitionCN: 幸好；日常同义词，语气更口语。

entries.definition: in a lucky or joyful way
entries.definitionCN: 幸运地；快乐地；可与 fortunately 互换但更强调愉悦。

entries.definition: as if arranged by a protecting power
entries.definitionCN: 似有天助地；书面语中表达「万幸」。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on fortune, the goddess, and the sentence use.
normalIntro.cn: 基于 fortune、命运女神与句子用法的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Remember the goddess Fortuna spinning her wheel of luck.
normal.cn: 记住命运女神 Fortuna 转动运气之轮。

normal.en: Fortune means luck: fortunate is lucky, fortunately is luckily.
normal.cn: fortune 是运气：fortunate 幸运的，fortunately 幸运地。

normal.en: Note the sentence pattern: Fortunately, no one was hurt.
normal.cn: 记住句式：Fortunately, no one was hurt（幸好无人受伤）。

normal.en: Contrast with unfortunately to lock in both words at once.
normal.cn: 与 unfortunately 对照，一次锁定两个词。

normal.en: Spot the family: fortune, fortunate, misfortune, fortunately.
normal.cn: 观察词族：fortune、fortunate、misfortune、fortunately。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel of fortune stopping on the winning color.
abstract.cn: 想象幸运轮盘停在中奖的颜色上。

abstract.en: Picture a net catching a falling cup just in time.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网及时接住了掉落的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture rain starting right after you step under a roof.
abstract.cn: 想象你刚进屋雨就开始下。

examples.en: Fortunately, the bus was late too, so we did not miss it.
examples.cn: 幸好公交车也晚点了，我们没错过。

examples.en: He fell off his bike, but fortunately he was not badly hurt.
examples.cn: 他从自行车上摔下来，所幸伤得不重。

examples.en: Fortunately for the team, their best player recovered in time.
examples.cn: 对全队来说幸运的是，最佳球员及时康复了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福车呢提」——运气这辆福车恰好停在门口等着你：fortunately 就是「好运及时赶到」。

root: fortunately 来自拉丁语 fors / Fortuna（运气、命运女神），经古法语 fortune 进入英语；fortunate（幸运的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成。词根的意象是「命运之轮转到好的一面」。

sensesIntro.en: Fortunately covers both lucky events and the speaker's relieved comment on them.
sensesIntro.cn: fortunately 既描述「因好运而发生的事」，也承载说话人「幸好、松了口气」的总评语气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the wheel of luck stopping on the good side
core.cn: 核心意象：命运之轮恰好转到好的一面

branches.en: A bad event was avoided by luck
branches.cn: 坏事因运气被躲过

branches.en: A good result arrived just in time
branches.cn: 好结果及时到来

branches.en: The whole sentence is marked as lucky
branches.cn: 副词给整句话盖上「幸好」的标记

branches.en: Speaker relief at a near miss
branches.cn: 说话人对擦身而过的危险的庆幸

branches.en: From event luck to commenting luck
branches.cn: 从「事件幸运」到「评注幸运」的延伸

intro.en: Fortunately is built with clear layers: fortune + -ate + -ly.
intro.cn: fortunately 结构层次清晰：fortune + -ate + -ly。

latinIntro.en: The root belongs to Latin fors and Fortuna, with Old French as the carrier.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属于拉丁语 fors 与 Fortuna，古法语是传入的桥梁。

items.example: She told her fortune with cards.
A fortuitous meeting changed his life.

items.exampleCN: 提示：此 fort 非彼 fort。

definition_zh: 告诉；讲述；吩咐；分辨；告发；显示；数；产生效果
definition_en: to give information by speech or writing, to narrate a story, to order someone to do something, or to be able to distinguish one thing from another
core_image: 一个人凑近另一个人的耳朵，话从口中流出
scene: 夜里孩子缠着母亲讲故事，母亲点了一盏小灯。 Grandmother told them a tale of the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 tell 是「讲述」（第 2 个义项：说出故事的内容）；句意：祖母给孩子们讲了一个大海的故事。

pos.zh: 告发；产生效果；（语言）显示

derivatives.zh: 讲述者；银行出纳员（由 tell 加表人后缀构成，指说话或点钞的人）
有说服力的；起作用的（现在分词转形容词，指话语产生效果）
算命者（复合词，tell 保留「预示、说出」义）

senses.title: Give information by speaking
senses.definition: to give information to someone in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面方式把信息告诉某人
senses.example: Tell me your address and I will send the parcel.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的地址告诉我，我把包裹寄出去。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply putting something into words for another person: speech is counted out to a listener.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是把某事用话点给别人听：话语像被「数给」听者。

senses.title: Narrate a story or events
senses.definition: to give an account of a story, or of events in order
senses.definitionCN: 依次讲出故事或事情的经过
senses.example: The grandmother told a tale of the old village.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母讲了一个老村庄的故事。
senses.why: Narration is information stretched into sequence: many small bits of telling are lined up into a whole.
senses.whyCN: 叙述是把信息拉长成序列：许多细小的「告知」连成整体，便成了故事。

senses.title: Order someone to do something
senses.definition: to say to someone that they must do something
senses.definitionCN: 要求或指示某人必须做某事
senses.example: The coach told us to warm up first.
senses.exampleCN: 教练吩咐我们先热身。
senses.why: Speech directed at someone becomes instruction; the telling carries weight, not just information.
senses.whyCN: 话语指向某人时就成了指令；此时的「说」带有分量，不只是传递信息。

senses.title: Distinguish one thing from another
senses.definition: to be able to know or judge the difference between things
senses.definitionCN: 能看出或判断出事物之间的差别
senses.example: I cannot tell the twins apart.
senses.exampleCN: 我分辨不出这对双胞胎。
senses.why: To tell here is to reckon or count out a difference, an old sense of counting that survives in judgment.
senses.whyCN: 此义里的 tell 是「点算」出差别——这是它古老的「数、计」义残留在判断里。

senses.title: Reveal an effect or a state
senses.definition: to show or reveal something, especially strain or age, without words
senses.definitionCN: 无需言语就显露出状况，尤指疲累或年岁
senses.example: The long journey was beginning to tell on his health.
senses.exampleCN: 长途跋涉开始影响他的健康。
senses.why: A state that cannot be hidden is itself telling: facts speak when people stay silent.
senses.whyCN: 藏不住的状态自己在「说话」：人不开口时，事实替他开口，便是 tell。

senses.title: Inform against someone
senses.definition: to report someone secretly to a person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 暗中向掌权者举报某人
senses.example: The boy was afraid his classmate would tell on him.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩怕同学告他的状。
senses.why: Telling takes a dark turn when the listener is authority: the same speech act becomes betrayal.
senses.whyCN: 当听话者变成权威，讲述就转向阴暗面：同一个说话动作成了告发。

senses.title: Count things one by one
senses.definition: to count objects or recite numbers in order, now mainly in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 逐一清点或顺次念数，今多见于固定短语
senses.example: The old phrase tells the beads one by one.
senses.exampleCN: 旧短语里一颗颗数念珠。
senses.why: This is the root sense: tell once meant simply to count, as it still does in teller and all told.
senses.whyCN: 这是词根义：tell 原本就是「数」，至今还活在 teller 与 all told 里。

intro.en: Tell is a native Germanic verb. Its oldest meaning is to count or reckon, from which telling others and telling stories both grew.
intro.cn: tell 是日耳曼本族动词，最古老的含义是「数、点算」，告知与讲故事都由此长出。

items.en: Tellan meant to count, reckon, or enumerate things one by one.
items.cn: 古英语 tellan 意为逐个清点、计算。

items.en: Talu, the related noun, gave both tale and tally, keeping the counting sense.
items.cn: 同源名词 talu 衍生出 tale 与 tally，保留了「数」义。

items.en: The verb goes back to a Germanic root for counting, cognate with German zählen.
items.cn: 动词可追溯至日耳曼语「计数」词根，与德语 zählen 同源。

items.en: The sense moved from counting things to counting out words: informing, narrating and ordering.
items.cn: 词义从「数物」移向「数话」：告知、叙述与吩咐相继出现。

items.en: Judging differences and revealing effects kept the reckoning image, while counting survives only in old phrases.
items.cn: 分辨与显效保留了「点算」意象，而「数」义只留在旧短语中。

note.en: Tell is set beside its Germanic relatives and beside speech verbs that overlap with it.
note.cn: 把 tell 与日耳曼同族词，以及与之交叠的言语动词放在一起对比。

entries.definition: a story, from the same Germanic counting root
entries.definitionCN: 故事；与 tell 同出「计数」词根

entries.definition: a running count or record
entries.definitionCN: 计数；记录，保留「点算」古义

entries.definition: a person who tells, or counts money at a bank
entries.definitionCN: 讲述者；银行出纳员

entries.definition: to speak words, without the sense of informing a particular person
entries.definitionCN: 说出话来，不含「告知特定对象」的意味

entries.definition: to give a spoken account of events in order
entries.definitionCN: 依次口述事件经过，更书面

entries.definition: to give someone facts, often official
entries.definitionCN: 告知事实，语气偏正式

normalIntro.en: Real links: the counting root, the tale family, the bank teller, and the phrase all told.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：计数词根、tale 词族、银行出纳与 all told 短语。

normal.en: Tell once meant to count; all told still means counted altogether.
normal.cn: tell 原义是数；all told 至今意为「总计清点」。

normal.en: Tale and tell are twins: a tale is something told.
normal.cn: tale 与 tell 是孪生兄弟：故事就是被讲述的东西。

normal.en: A bank teller literally counts money for you.
normal.cn: 银行出纳员 teller 字面上就是替你数钱的人。

normal.en: Tell the twins apart: count out the difference between them.
normal.cn: tell the twins apart：把两人之间的差别「点算」出来。

normal.en: Tell on him: your words reach the teacher, and the counting turns into blame.
normal.cn: tell on him：你的话传到老师那里，「点算」变成了指责。

abstract.en: Every sentence is a small counting: word after word handed to a listener.
abstract.cn: 每句话都是一次小小的清点：一个词接一个词递给听者。

abstract.en: Silence also tells: what cannot be hidden speaks by itself.
abstract.cn: 沉默也会说话：藏不住的东西自己开口。

abstract.en: Stories are counted-out time, bead after bead.
abstract.cn: 故事是被一颗颗数出的时光。

examples.en: She told me the truth about the missing key.
examples.cn: 她把钥匙失踪的真相告诉了我。

examples.en: Grandfather told the same story every winter night.
examples.cn: 祖父每年冬夜都讲同一个故事。

examples.en: The strain of the exams is telling on her.
examples.cn: 考试的压力正在影响她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太欧」——太欧（tel）老师一遍遍数着欧几里得的题，数着数着就讲给你听 → tell 数、讲、告诉

root: 日耳曼本族动词：古英语 tellan「数、点算」，同根名词 talu 给出 tale 与 tally；「告知、讲述」由「逐一数出」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From counting things, tell grew into counting out words to a listener, and finally into silent facts that speak.
sensesIntro.cn: tell 从数物出发，长出向听者「数话」的告知与讲述，最终连无声的事实也会 tell。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: counting things out one by one, then counting out words.
core.cn: 核心意象：逐一点数，再逐词「点数」给听者。

branches.en: The root sense survives in old phrases.
branches.cn: 词根义存活于旧短语。

branches.en: Information handed over word by word.
branches.cn: 信息被逐词递交。

branches.en: Many tellings lined up become a story.
branches.cn: 许多次讲述连缀成故事。

branches.en: Speech aimed at a person turns to order or to betrayal.
branches.cn: 指向某人的话语变成命令或告发。

branches.en: Reckoning a difference; facts that speak unbidden.
branches.cn: 点算差别；事实不请自言。

intro.en: Tell belongs to the Germanic counting family shared with tale, tally and talk.
intro.cn: tell 属日耳曼「计数」词族，与 tale、tally、talk 同源相关。

latinIntro.en: Tell is not from Latin; the nearest Latin parallels are reckoning verbs, given here only as contrast.
latinIntro.cn: tell 并非源自拉丁语；此处列出拉丁语中的「计算」动词仅作对照。

items.exampleCN: talu 衍生 tale 与 tally。

items.meaningCN: 数；计算（拉丁来源的对照词）

definition_zh: 踢；踢球；踢腿；戒除（习惯）；刺激；乐趣
definition_en: to hit something with the foot, or to end a habit, usually with effort
core_image: 一只脚猛地抬起，鞋尖撞在球面上，球飞了出去
scene: 球场边风很冷，少年把球抛起，抬腿一脚，球穿过整片草地。 He kicked the ball over the fence and climbed after it.
sceneCN: 这里 kick 是「踢」（第 1 个义项：用脚击打），句意为他把球踢过篱笆，又爬过去捡。画面里的物件：球场、草地、篱笆。

pos.zh: 动词：踢；踢球；戒除；（枪）后坐

derivatives.zh: 由 kick 加 -er 构成，指踢球的人或（美式足球）踢球员
由 kick 加 -ing 构成，义为「活泼的；带劲的」

senses.title: To hit with the foot
senses.definition: to strike something with the foot or feet
senses.definitionCN: 用一只或两只脚击打某物
senses.example: She kicked the door open with one foot.
senses.exampleCN: 她一脚把门踹开了。
senses.why: The core act is one sudden blow delivered by a leg.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是腿发出的一记突然打击。

senses.title: To move a ball by foot
senses.definition: to send a ball through the air with the foot, as in a game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中用脚把球踢出去
senses.example: He kicked the ball straight into the net.
senses.exampleCN: 他直接把球踢进了网里。
senses.why: A ball is the object most often sent away by that blow.
senses.whyCN: 被这一击送走的物件里，球最常见。

senses.title: To thrust a leg
senses.definition: to move the legs sharply, as in swimming or dancing
senses.definitionCN: 在游泳或跳舞中快速蹬腿
senses.example: The baby kicked and laughed in the bath.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在洗澡水里蹬着腿笑。
senses.why: Legs also kick without hitting anything, as in water.
senses.whyCN: 腿也会空踢，比如在水里。

senses.title: To give up a habit
senses.definition: to stop doing something habitual, often with struggle
senses.definitionCN: 指停止某个习惯，往往经过一番挣扎
senses.example: It took him three tries to kick the smoking habit.
senses.exampleCN: 他试了三次才戒掉抽烟。
senses.why: Giving up a habit is pictured as kicking it away from you.
senses.whyCN: 戒掉习惯被画成把它从身边踢开。

senses.title: A sharp thrill
senses.definition: a feeling of excitement or amusement from something
senses.definitionCN: 从某事得到的兴奋或愉悦
senses.example: She gets a kick out of fixing old bikes.
senses.exampleCN: 她从修旧自行车里得到乐趣。
senses.why: Excitement is a blow felt inside rather than outside.
senses.whyCN: 兴奋是在身体里感到的一记击打。

senses.title: The recoil of a gun
senses.definition: the backward push of a firearm when fired
senses.definitionCN: 枪射击时向后的推力
senses.example: The rifle has a strong kick.
senses.exampleCN: 这把步枪后坐力很大。
senses.why: A gun pushes back exactly where a foot would push.
senses.whyCN: 枪向后推的位置，正是脚会推的位置。

intro.en: Kick is a Middle English word of uncertain origin, probably imitative of the blow it names.
intro.cn: kick 是中古英语词，来源不详，很可能模仿踢击的声音与动作。

items.en: kicken appeared in the fourteenth century meaning to strike with the foot.
items.cn: kicken 十四世纪出现，意为用脚击打。

items.en: No certain source is known; it may echo the sound of a blow.
items.cn: 确切来源不明，可能模仿击打的声音。

items.en: The ball-game sense spread with modern football.
items.cn: 球类比赛的「踢球」义随现代足球传播。

items.en: Kick the habit, meaning to stop, dates from the twentieth century.
items.cn: 表示戒除的 kick the habit 出现于二十世纪。

items.en: The noun kick for excitement grew from drink and sport slang.

entries.definition: To hit something hard.

entries.definition: To drop a ball and kick it before it lands.
entries.definitionCN: 指落下前把球踢出的动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a foot striking a ball to the recoil of a rifle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从脚踢中球走到步枪的后坐。

normal.en: Kick is probably imitative, echoing the impact itself.

normal.en: Kick off starts a match and also a project.
normal.cn: kick off 既开球，也开启一个项目。

normal.en: Kick the habit means to stop for good.

normal.en: Get a kick out of means enjoy it a great deal.

normal.en: Kicked is the past form; there is no kickt.

abstract.cn: 踢是用脚做出的一个突然决定。

abstract.en: The same word shakes off a ball and shakes off a habit.

abstract.en: Excitement and recoil are both a backward push.

core.cn: 核心意象：脚猛地向前打中眼前的东西。

branches.cn: 最后一支烟这条线：把习惯踢掉。

branches.cn: 肩膀这条线：打中的东西回推你。
