definition_zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；防备
definition_en: to give or supply something that is needed, to state a rule in a law or contract, or to support someone with money
core_image: 旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，再转身把干粮和水递给身后的人
scene: 洪水退去后的第三天，村口的空地上支起几张长桌，志愿者把水和面包摆成一排。 The relief team came to provide blankets and hot food for the flooded villages.
sceneCN: 这里取「提供、供给」的意思（第 1 个义项：把别人需要的东西给出去）；句意为救援队来为受淹的村庄提供毛毯和热食。村口长桌上摆开的水和面包就是线索。

pos.zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；为…做准备

derivatives.zh: 由 provide 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「供应者；提供者」
由拉丁语名词 provisio（预见、照料）经法语进入英语，义为「供应；条款；储备」
由拉丁词干 provid- 加 -ent 构成，义为「有远见的；用钱谨慎的」
由过去分词转成的连词，义为「假如；只要」，常见于 provided that

senses.title: To supply something that is needed
senses.definition: to give someone something they need or to make something available for use
senses.definitionCN: 把别人需要的东西给出去，或使某物可供使用
senses.example: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。
senses.why: Latin providere joins pro-, ahead, to videre, to see; seeing ahead means noticing a need before it arrives, and the next move is to get the thing ready and hand it over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 providere 把表示「在前」的 pro- 接在 videre（看）上：提前看见，就是在需求到来之前先察觉；察觉之后最自然的动作，就是把东西备好递过去，于是「预先看见」变成了「供给」。

senses.title: To state as a rule in a law or contract
senses.definition: to establish a rule or condition in a law, contract or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、合同或协议中确立某条规则或条件
senses.example: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。
senses.why: A rule written in advance is itself a kind of foresight: the text settles now what will happen later, so the verb that means to get ready also names what a document lays down beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 提前写好的条文本身就是一种预见：文本在此刻就决定了以后会发生什么，所以那个表示「预先备好」的动词，也用来指文件事先订下的内容。

senses.title: To support someone financially
senses.definition: to earn the money that allows another person, especially a family member, to live
senses.definitionCN: 挣钱供另一个人生活，尤指供养家庭成员
senses.example: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
senses.exampleCN: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。
senses.why: Providing for someone is looking ahead on their behalf: the money is set aside before the need is felt, which is the household version of seeing ahead.
senses.whyCN: 供养一个人，就是替对方往前看：钱在需求出现之前就留出来，这正是「预先看见」在家庭里的样子。

senses.title: To make preparation against something
senses.definition: to take action in advance so that a possible problem or danger does less harm
senses.definitionCN: 提前采取行动，使可能出现的问题或危险危害更小
senses.example: They built the wall to provide against flooding in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修了这道墙，用来防备春季洪水。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is pure foresight with nothing given away: to provide against a risk is to see it coming and move before it lands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是纯粹的「预先看见」，与给东西无关：provide against 某个风险，就是看出它会来，并在它落地之前先动手。

intro.en: Provide is built from two Latin pieces meaning ahead and to see, and that single image of foresight later spreads into supply, legal rules and family support.
intro.cn: provide 由两个拉丁语成分构成，意思分别是「在前」和「看」；这一「预先看见」的画面后来扩展到供给、法律条文与养家。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and it supplied the visual core of a large family of Latin words.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，为一大族拉丁词提供了「看」这个核心。

items.en: Pro- meant ahead or in front, so providere meant to see ahead, to foresee and to take care of something in advance.
items.cn: pro- 表示「在前、预先」，所以 providere 意为往前看、预见，并提前照管某事。

items.en: The noun providentia named foresight and careful management, and it survives in the English words providence and provident.
items.cn: 名词 providentia 指远见与谨慎的照料，它留在英语的 providence 与 provident 里。

items.en: Old French pourveoir kept both halves of the meaning: to foresee a need and to supply what it calls for.
items.cn: 古法语 pourveoir 保留了两半意思：既预见需求，也提供需求所需的东西。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as provide and carried the word into law, where a document provides, and into the household, where a wage provides for a family.
items.cn: 英语把拼写固定为 provide，并把这个词带进法律——文件可以「规定」，也带进家庭——工资可以「养家」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving what is needed.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示「给出所需之物」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for supplying something, and also a clause in a document.
entries.definitionCN: 表示供应之事的名字，也指文件中的条款。

entries.definition: Care or guidance that looks ahead, often attributed to a higher power.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来作准备的照管，常被归于更高的力量。

entries.definition: Careful about the future, especially with money.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来打算的，尤指用钱谨慎的。

entries.definition: A person or a company that supplies something.
entries.definitionCN: 提供某物的人或机构。

entries.definition: To give or sell what is needed over time.
entries.definitionCN: 持续提供或出售所需之物。

entries.definition: To provide furniture or whatever else is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 提供家具或所需之物。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to take.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西拿出来供人取用。

entries.definition: To supply with tools or skills for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的提供工具或技能。

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a look into the future, not with a gift, and its family keeps returning to foresight, readiness and the handover that follows.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是送礼；同族词反复回到预见、准备以及随之而来的交付。

normal.en: Pro- means ahead and videre means to see, so provide begins with a look into the future rather than with an object.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前」，videre 意为「看」，所以 provide 的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是某件东西。

normal.en: Provision is the noun built on the same stem: what has been seen ahead and therefore got ready.
normal.cn: provision 是同一词干上的名词：预先看见、因此备好的东西。

normal.en: The legal use, as in the law provides, works because a written rule also decides the future in advance.
normal.cn: 法律用法如 the law provides 之所以成立，是因为写下的规则同样在提前决定未来。

normal.en: Provider adds -er, the person who does the providing, exactly as in employer and adviser.
normal.cn: provider 加 -er，指做「提供」这件事的人，与 employer、adviser 的构造相同。

normal.en: Provided that keeps the past participle and turns it into a condition: if this is seen to, the rest follows.
normal.cn: provided that 保留过去分词形式，把它变成条件：只要这一点被照看到，其余便随之成立。

abstract.en: To provide is to act on a future you have already seen, which is why the word sounds like care more than charity.
abstract.cn: 提供是对一个你已经看见的未来采取行动，所以这个词听起来更像照料，而不像施舍。

abstract.en: A law that provides and a parent who provides are doing one thing: fixing tomorrow before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 法律规定与父母供养做的是同一件事：在明天到来之前就把它安排下来。

abstract.en: The whole word lives in the gap between seeing a need and meeting it.
abstract.cn: 从看见需求到满足需求之间的那段距离，正是这个词的全部所在。

examples.en: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
examples.cn: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。

examples.en: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
examples.cn: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。

examples.en: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
examples.cn: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若外德」——听着像「铺好喂的」，先把吃的用的铺好喂到人跟前，正是提供。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前、预先）+ videre（看见）构成 providere，本义「预先看到、提前照管」，由此引申为「预备、供给、规定、供养」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is foresight; the senses divide into supplying a need, writing a rule down, supporting a family, and guarding against a risk.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「预先看见」；义项分成满足需求、把规则写下来、供养家人，以及防备风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller standing on a rise, looking far down the road, then turning back to hand food and water to those behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，然后转身把干粮和水递给身后的人。

branches.en: a table of food laid out before anyone asks
branches.cn: 没人开口前就摆好的一桌食物

branches.en: a clause printed in small type at the end of a contract
branches.cn: 合同末尾用小字印出的条款

branches.en: a wage that keeps an old couple fed
branches.cn: 让一对老人吃得上饭的一份工资

branches.en: a wall raised before the river rises
branches.cn: 河水上涨之前就砌起的墙

branches.en: a store of grain kept for a bad year
branches.cn: 为荒年留下的存粮

intro.en: A Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of seeing hold the word together, and French reshaped the verb before English took it.
intro.cn: 表示向前的拉丁语前缀与表示「看见」的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，法语先在中间改造了动词形式，英语随后借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, the compound providere, to see ahead, and the noun providentia, foresight, are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）、复合形式 providere（往前看）与名词 providentia（远见）是英语这个词的直接来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to see ahead, to take care

definition_zh: 放置；设置；树立；凝固；一套
definition_en: to put something in place, to adjust equipment, to establish something, to become solid, or a group of things used together
core_image: 闹钟被放到床头，指针停在六点
scene: 她把花瓶放在桌上。 She set the vase on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 set 是「放置」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把花瓶放在桌上。

derivatives.zh: 环境；设置
预置
重置
抵消；补偿

senses.title: To place
senses.definition: to put something in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到特定位置
senses.example: She set the vase on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她把花瓶放在桌上。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To adjust
senses.definition: to adjust a device or arrange something in advance
senses.definitionCN: 调整装置或预先安排好
senses.example: He set the alarm for six.
senses.exampleCN: 他把闹钟设在六点。
senses.why: Setting a device is placing its state.
senses.whyCN: 设置装置就是安放它的状态。

senses.title: To establish
senses.definition: to establish a record, rule, or example
senses.definitionCN: 创下纪录、定下规则或树立榜样
senses.example: The team set a new record.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍创下了新纪录。
senses.why: An idea can be placed firmly too.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能被牢牢安放。

senses.title: To become solid
senses.definition: to become solid or fixed
senses.definitionCN: 变成固体或固定下来
senses.example: The jelly will set in the fridge.
senses.exampleCN: 果冻会在冰箱里凝固。
senses.why: A liquid takes a fixed shape.
senses.whyCN: 液体固定成一种形状。

senses.title: A group of things
senses.definition: a group of things that belong together
senses.definitionCN: 配套的一组东西
senses.example: She bought a set of tools.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一套工具。
senses.why: The noun names things placed together.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set comes from Old English settan, to cause to sit, from the same root as sit.
intro.cn: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），与 sit 同根。

items.en: Satjan meant to cause to sit.
items.cn: satjan 意为使坐下。

items.en: Settan meant to place or set.
items.cn: settan 意为放置、安放。

items.en: Set kept its placing sense.
items.cn: set 保留了放置的含义。

items.en: Set extended to devices and records.
items.cn: set 扩展到装置设置与纪录。

items.en: The noun named a matched group.
items.cn: 名词形式指配套的一组。

note.en: Set is compared with similar-looking words and with words for placing.
note.cn: 把 set 与形近词以及表示放置的词作比较。

entries.definition: to rest on a seat

entries.definition: a place to sit
entries.definitionCN: 座位

entries.definition: to allow
entries.definitionCN: 让；允许

entries.definition: to place something
entries.definitionCN: 放置

entries.definition: to change slightly
entries.definitionCN: 调整

entries.definition: to set up firmly
entries.definitionCN: 建立

normalIntro.en: Set is the act of causing something to sit: an object, a clock, a record, or a liquid.
normalIntro.cn: set 就是让某物「坐下」：一个物件、一只钟、一项纪录或一种液体。

normal.en: Set the cup on the shelf.
normal.cn: 把杯子放到架子上。

normal.en: Set the alarm before bed.
normal.cn: 睡前设好闹钟。

normal.en: They set a record in the relay.
normal.cn: 他们在接力赛中创下纪录。

normal.en: Leave the cement to set.
normal.cn: 让水泥慢慢凝固。

normal.en: This set of dishes has six plates.
normal.cn: 这套餐具共有六个盘子。

abstract.en: To set something is to decide where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 安放某物，就是决定它该在哪里。

abstract.en: A record is a moment set into history.
abstract.cn: 纪录，是被安放进历史的一刻。

abstract.en: Some things set only when we stop holding them.
abstract.cn: 有些东西，只有我们松手后才会定型。

examples.en: She set the vase on the table.
examples.cn: 她把花瓶放在桌上。

examples.en: He set the alarm for six.
examples.cn: 他把闹钟设在六点。

examples.en: The jelly will set in the fridge.
examples.cn: 果冻会在冰箱里凝固。

dict_mnemonic.text: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），核心义「把东西安放到某个位置」，引申出设置、树立、凝固与一套。

root: 源自古英语 settan（使坐下、安放），与 sit 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Set means to place, adjust, establish, become solid, or a matched group.
sensesIntro.cn: set 意为放置、设置、树立、凝固或一套。

core.en: Causing something to take a fixed place.
core.cn: 使某物占据一个固定的位置。

branches.en: Putting an object down.
branches.cn: 把物件放下。

branches.en: Arranging a device.
branches.cn: 把装置调好。

branches.en: Fixing a record or rule.
branches.cn: 把纪录或规则定下。

branches.en: A liquid taking shape.
branches.cn: 液体成形。

branches.en: Things placed together.
branches.cn: 被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set is a short native verb that joins with prefixes to make many new words.
intro.cn: set 是简短的日耳曼语本族动词，能与前缀组合出许多新词。

latinIntro.cn: set 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ponere（放置）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She sets the table every night.

items.exampleCN: 烤箱预设为一百八十度。

items.example: Reset the clock after the power cut.

items.meaning: to balance one effect with another
items.exampleCN: 节省抵消了更高的成本。

items.example: The setter placed the ball well.

senses.title: The inner self
senses.definition: the part of a person that is not the body
senses.definitionCN: 人身上不属于肉体的部分
senses.example: Her spirit remained strong after the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 病后她的精神依然坚强。
senses.why: The core sense is the inner, non-physical self.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项，指内在而非肉体的自我。

senses.title: Mood or morale
senses.definition: the mood or feeling of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体的情绪与士气
senses.example: The team faced the challenge in high spirits.
senses.exampleCN: 团队情绪高涨地迎接挑战。
senses.why: The inner state is seen from outside as mood.
senses.whyCN: 把内在状态外化为可观察的情绪。

senses.title: A ghost
senses.definition: a ghost or unseen being
senses.definitionCN: 鬼魂或看不见的存在
senses.example: The old house is said to have a spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 据说老房子里有幽灵。
senses.why: A bodiless being is the oldest extended sense.
senses.whyCN: 没有肉体的存在，是最古老的引申义。

intro.en: Spirit goes back to Latin spiritus, meaning breath.
intro.cn: spirit 可追溯到拉丁语 spiritus，意为气息。

items.en: Spiritus meant breath and the breath of life.
items.cn: spiritus 意为气息与生命之气。

items.en: Espirit carried the sense of soul and courage.
items.cn: espirit 带有灵魂与勇气的含义。

items.en: Spirit named the soul and invisible beings.
items.cn: spirit 指灵魂与看不见的存在。

items.en: The word also came to mean mood and morale.
items.cn: 这个词又发展出情绪与士气的含义。

items.en: Spirits named strong drink in the plural.
items.cn: 复数 spirits 又指烈酒。

note.en: Spirit is compared with look-alike words and words for the inner self.
note.cn: 把 spirit 与形近词以及表示内在自我的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spirit is breath that outlasts the body.
normalIntro.cn: spirit 是比肉体活得更久的那口气。

normal.en: She has a strong spirit.
normal.cn: 她有坚强的精神。

normal.en: The team showed great spirit.
normal.cn: 这支队伍表现出极佳的士气。

normal.en: He was in low spirits.
normal.cn: 他情绪低落。

normal.en: They believe in the human spirit.
normal.cn: 他们相信人的精神。

normal.en: The story is about a wandering spirit.
normal.cn: 这故事讲的是一个游荡的幽灵。

abstract.en: The body is a room; the spirit is the light in it.
abstract.cn: 身体是房间，精神是里面的光。

abstract.en: Morale rises and falls like a tide.
abstract.cn: 士气像潮水一样涨落。

abstract.en: What has no body can still be felt.
abstract.cn: 没有形体的东西，依然能被感到。

examples.en: Her spirit remained strong after the illness.
examples.cn: 病后她的精神依然坚强。

examples.en: The team faced the challenge in high spirits.
examples.cn: 团队情绪高涨地迎接挑战。

examples.en: The old house is said to have a spirit.
examples.cn: 据说老房子里有幽灵。

dict_mnemonic.text: spirit 源自拉丁语 spiritus（气息），与 inspire（吸气、鼓舞）、respiration（呼吸）同根；team spirit 是团队精神，in high spirits 是情绪高涨，复数 spirits 还可指烈酒。

root: 来自拉丁语 spiritus（气息、呼吸），经古法语 espirit 进入英语，核心义为「生命之气」，后扩展为精神、情绪与幽灵。

sensesIntro.en: Spirit means the inner self, a mood or morale, or a ghost.
sensesIntro.cn: spirit 指内在的自我、情绪士气，或幽灵。

core.en: Breath that carries life and self.
core.cn: 承载生命与自我的气息。

branches.en: A quiet breath rises in the chest.
branches.cn: 一次安静的呼吸在胸口升起。

branches.en: A crowd lifts its voice together.
branches.cn: 人群一起提高了声音。

branches.en: A pale shape passes through a wall.
branches.cn: 一个苍白的影子穿过墙壁。

branches.en: The inner self shows itself as mood.
branches.cn: 内在的自我，以外在情绪显现。

branches.en: Both mood and ghost are felt, not touched.
branches.cn: 情绪与幽灵，都只能感到，不能触摸。

intro.en: Spirit forms adjectives, adverbs, and abstract nouns.
intro.cn: spirit 构成形容词、副词和抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is spiritus, breath.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 spiritus，意为气息。

scene: 我明天会给你打电话。 I shall call you tomorrow.

senses.title: Future with I or we
senses.definition: used with I or we to talk about the future
senses.definitionCN: 与 I 或 we 连用，表示将来
senses.example: I shall call you tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 我明天会给你打电话。
senses.why: This is the traditional future use.
senses.whyCN: 这是传统的将来时用法。

senses.title: Must in rules
senses.definition: used in official rules to mean must
senses.definitionCN: 在正式规定中表示「必须」
senses.example: Students shall not smoke on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 学生不得在校园内吸烟。
senses.why: Law and rules use shall for obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律与规章用 shall 表示义务。

senses.title: Offer or suggestion
senses.definition: used in questions to offer something or suggest an action
senses.definitionCN: 在疑问句中用于提供某物或建议行动
senses.example: Shall we go for a walk?
senses.exampleCN: 我们去散散步好吗？
senses.why: The question asks for agreement.
senses.whyCN: 这种疑问句在征求同意。

intro.en: Shall comes from Old English sceal, meaning owe or must, and softened into a future marker.
intro.cn: shall 源自古英语 sceal（欠、必须），后来弱化为将来时的标记。

items.en: Skal meant I owe or I must.
items.cn: skal 意为「我欠」或「我必须」。

items.en: Sceal meant must or ought.
items.cn: sceal 意为必须或应当。

items.en: Shall marked duty and future.
items.cn: shall 同时标记义务与将来。

items.en: Shall became a future helper with I and we.
items.cn: shall 成为与 I、we 连用的将来助动词。

items.en: Rules kept shall for obligation.
items.cn: 规章保留了 shall 的义务含义。

note.en: Shall is compared with similar-looking words and with other modal verbs.
note.cn: 把 shall 与形近词以及其他情态动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shall began as a word for owing and became a gentle way to mark the future or a rule.
normalIntro.cn: shall 最初表示「欠」，后来变成标记将来或规定的温和方式。

normal.en: I shall see you next week.
normal.cn: 我下周见你。

normal.en: We shall need more time.
normal.cn: 我们将需要更多时间。

normal.en: The rule says visitors shall sign in.
normal.cn: 规定说访客须登记。

normal.en: Shall I open the window?
normal.cn: 我打开窗户好吗？

normal.en: Shall we begin?
normal.cn: 我们开始吧？

abstract.en: A word of obligation can soften into a word of invitation.
abstract.cn: 一个表示义务的词，也能软化成邀请。

abstract.en: The future is often spoken as a promise.
abstract.cn: 将来，常常是被当作承诺说出来的。

abstract.en: Rules sound gentler when they use an old, quiet word.
abstract.cn: 用上一个古老而安静的词，规定也会显得温和。

examples.en: I shall call you tomorrow.
examples.cn: 我明天会给你打电话。

examples.en: Students shall not smoke on campus.
examples.cn: 学生不得在校园内吸烟。

examples.en: Shall we go for a walk?
examples.cn: 我们去散散步好吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: shall 源自古英语 sceal（必须、应当），后来成为表示将来、规定与提议的情态动词。

root: 源自古英语 sceal（欠、必须），与 should 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shall marks the future with I or we, obligation in rules, or a polite offer.
sensesIntro.cn: shall 表示与 I、we 连用的将来、规章中的义务或礼貌的提议。

core.en: A modal word that moves from owing to intending.
core.cn: 从「欠」走向「打算」的情态词。

branches.en: A future spoken with I or we.
branches.cn: 与 I 或 we 连用的将来。

branches.en: An obligation written in rules.
branches.cn: 写进规章的义务。

branches.en: A question that offers or suggests.
branches.cn: 提供或建议的疑问句。

branches.en: Promise and duty share one form.
branches.cn: 承诺与义务共用一个形式。

branches.en: The same word can command or invite.
branches.cn: 同一个词既能命令，也能邀请。

intro.en: Shall belongs to the old Germanic modal verbs, with should as its past form.
intro.cn: shall 属于古老的日耳曼语情态动词，should 是它的过去式形式。

latinIntro.en: Shall has no Latin ancestor; Latin debere, to owe, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shall 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 debere（欠、应当）只是语义对应词。
